Honestly, probably my favorite game of 2015 and will stay that way for a while. People always complain about the performance and the story and that its repetitive and boring. So here's a serious review, talking about the aspect that
actually matter in a video game. Lets get started:
Graphics: Looks amazing. Nothing else to say. If you say this game doesnt look fantastic you either have a toaster as a PC (in which case you shouldnt have even bought it to begin with, but we'll talk about that later) or you just cant tell between a good graphics game and a bad one. The explosions make me feel like Im in the game, and Im the one CAUSING them. Its honestly one of the most amazing experiences I have had with a video game.
Performance: So this is the main complain about the game. I dont know how it is on AMD (heard its crap tho) so I'll only talk about how it is for me. My build is a GTX 950 with an I5-4460 core (we will ignore other stats for now, as they dont matter as much). At first, I was worried I wouldnt be able to run it at all after seeing my build is under the minimum, and yes, on the first run I had 30 FPS while just playing and 15FPS while explosions were happening. So obviously, that was CRAP. No one likes to play a game on♥♥♥♥♥♥FPS. Even on the lowest graphics I had 40FPS, no more. But then, I messed with the settings and wasn't surprised to find that the V-Sync (Vertical Sync in the graphics settings) in this game absolutely DEMOLISHES the FPS. After turning V-Sync off, I'm now able to play with most setting on High and overall high graphics, and enjoy 60FPS with or without explosions. Just use the settings, and find what makes your Graphics Card pay for the loss of quality with good performance. And if your card is worse than the GTX 950, I honestly wouldnt even bother purchasing the game, just use the money and save up some more to upgrade. If you want to try it anyways, dont blame the game for running like♥♥♥♥♥♥ New games require newer technologies. Ok? ok.
Story: I haven't went through too much of the story as of right now, but at the moment I do think that, yes, its missing some stuff and it has much more potential in its story, and its not something Im interesting to know how it ends because it obviously is going to end Rico taking over the country. BUT, this isnt the reason I bought the game. I bought it for the FUN. It seems as if some people forgot what video games are for. THEY ARE MADE TO ENJOY THEM. If you dont like mostly messing about and just doing whatever the ♥♥♥♥ you want, then this isnt the game for you. But if you do, this is the PERFECT game for you, because you can do whatever you want to do. I spent half my time playing the game flying around grappling onto♥♥♥♥♥♥and training with the wingsuit, and honestly I think I can keep doing just this for another 200 hours. This game is amazing and has some amazing mechanics, I absolutely LOVE it.
TL;DR: Amazing game if you want to have FUN, not so good if you want a good story (can't run on a toaster, not even a brand new one).
Have fun! And remember to blow up everything, why? Just 'cause.

OK. This is how this review will go. First I will state my general thought of Just Cause 3, then I will list pros and cons, then i will dive much further into detail and then finally say some things I think should have been in the game.
First if all, I adore Just Cause 3, it is easily the best game of 2015 for me. (I haven't played the Witcher 3 yet though.)
PROS:
- Beautiful, and huge map.
- Great aesthetics.
- Better storyline than Just Cause 2.
- Trains :D
- Great choice of vehicles.
- Driving is pretty damn great.
- Etc...
CONS:
- Lots of the map is empty terrain.
- No multiplayer (Mod coming soon :D)
- Storyline is not as good as it could be (it is a just cause game though.)
- After you 100% complete the game, there is not much more to do.
Now, I will go into much more detail about these factors.
THE MAP:
Medici is a beautiful mediterranean paradise filled with things to see and do. Unfortunately, many parts of the map are under devoloped, like Insula Striate, which is the largest island, has few cities and towns besides the southern coastline and has lots of empty space. I think Avalanche could've taken the time to fill Insula Striate with many more towns and cites, in the mountains and on the northern coast. I also think they should've added more islands to the south west part of the ocean as well. I'll give the map a 7/10
AESTHETICS AND GRAPHICS:
Just Cause 3 may not have as good graphics as some of the other releases this year, *cough* EA Battlefront *cough* but I really think that the game looks great and handles pretty damn good on my PC (Specs listed at the bottom of the review). The light and colourful aesthetic along with the cheery music really makes a mediterrean island that works. Aesthetics: 10/10 Graphics 8.5/10
STORYLINE:
Just Cause 3 has a much better storyline than Just Cause 2, with characters you care about and laugh about, and some really fun missions. (I won't go into to much detail because I don't want to spoil the plot.) It may not be on the story telling calibar of a Telltale game or a Netflix original series, but it is damn good for a game about flying around in a squirrel suit blowing up bridges.  7/10
VEHICLES:
Just Cause 3 offers a great variety of vehicles from F1 race cars to cargo planes. The cargo plane and the transport boat are really cool because they can hold vehicles, which will allow for all out wars to happen in multiplayer, or you could just reanact the plane scene from Furious 7. One thing I think they missed out on was enabling the semi truck to pull trailers, you could fill with people or vehicles, for use with the rebels in singleplayer or with your friends in multiplayer. Also the Urga Fura's description says it can fit 12 people but it cant. :(      And this time around, unlike Just Cause 2, the vehicles dont look like crumpled paper when they are damaged. Trains are cool but I think they should be longer, faster and maybe have different types, like military transport, passenger trains, and rebel trains. All the cars handle great and drifting works fine, all in all a 8.5/10
POST-COMPLETION:
This section will almost be redundent after the multiplayer comes out, but Just Cause 3, has no post-game what so ever. And by this I mean post-100%, not post-story. After post-story, you still have to take over the rest of the map, which by the way I recommend not rushing to take over everything or else the game will get quite boring because there will be almost no military, and find all the collectibles to unlock everything. But after you have done all these things, the game becomes very boring because there is nothing to do. In the mean time I have replayed the game to the point where I have beat the story and used mods to get everything in the game, but I've left most of the map military-controlled. Until multiplayer comes out there is not much we can do about this. Post-game/story: 5/10
At this point if I averaged out all the scores, the game would get a measly 7.2/10 which is actually better than most reviewers gave it.
But heres the thing, lots of those review companies didn't really play the game to its most potential, the memories I will have of being slingshotted across the map inside my jeep because of a glitchy train, or seeing a jet randomly come flying out of the ground, or the first time I drove the F1 car, or laughing at Mario's lines, make up for some of the flaws. For just all around fun i give the game a solid 10/10, but heres the thing. That would still give the game a 7.6/10 which I do not believe is accurate. So ♥♥♥♥ THE MATH.
I give Just Cause 3 an 8.8/10 and with some of the approvements I have suggested it could easily be a 9.5/10.
I recommend Just Cause 3 with every cell in my brain. Game of the ♥♥♥♥ing year.
TL:DR Great game, slightly empty map, good cars, 8.8/10.
EDIT: David Tennant voices himself, as a kidnapped radio host. 10/10
EDIT ALMOST A YEAR LATER: The DLC's have improved the game further, making the map less empty, and adding more content. It runs better than it used to, but, after playing the Witcher 3, it is now my second favorite game from 2015, cause the Witcher is just so damn good. Nano's Multiplayer will be out soon :) I also take back my statement about it having good driving, the driving feels weird and heavy, but i also feel its better than the previous game.

With the release of Rome Total 2 - Emperor Edition, I think it's fairly safe to say the game is finally finished. After a rather dismal start the developers have been pushing the patches through, addressing the major problems of the game, such as siege AI and diplomacy (fixed in the latest patch), that made the game difficult to enjoy.
As someone who jumped straight from Rome 1/Medieval Total War because sadly, I had an old imac for about six years straight into Rome 2, I was baffled to say the least. However once I got used to the interface, food/public order and the diplomacy, I had a fantastic time. The game looks and sounds wonderful (Though I did get the Rome 1 Soundtrack mod) from it's dynamic cities to watching your men hack down the enemy in bloody fashion. The province system is cool as it makes you feel that you really have to fight to secure lands and play it smart when it comes to building and recruiting. The combat has been improved even further in this patch by slowing down the fights thus making casualties more frequent and taking the risk of going into battle on the open field an actual concern much like it was in real life.
Also, if you have an issue with any aspect of the game, you can probably find a mod for it made by a very active modding community. Personally I am a huge advocat of mod support for games.
Anyway, while this review wasn't the most detailed, I do reccomend you try the game if you haven't played it yet and/or returning to the series. I do feel it's a great game in a genre that I think should require some more attention because hey, who doesn't want to be the next Caesar (without the whole assasination thing of course)?

The Evil Within 2 is great, cannot reccomend it enough. It has some optimization issues with high end nvidia cards for some reason, but that doesn't seem to apply to everyone with those cards anyways. Unfortunately with stuff like this, the only people who post about it are the people having issues, obivously no one is making threads like "hey, just checking in to say that TEW2 works great on my card".
Anyways, it is both a return to form and an upgrade on the genre. I grew up playing Silent Hill and the original Resident Evil on the PS1.  Not only did these games really get me into gaming, but they also solidified what my favorite genre would be throughout my whole life. As time went on, these games started to get more linear and linear in the gameplay, obviously the story was almost always linear because of the genre itself but the gameplay turned into being thrown into a hallway, or being thrown into a small map and going from area to area, starting in a forest, going to a big facility, going underground maybe, idk. But it didn't start that way, going back to the original Silent Hill games and the first Resident Evil, you were thrown into one pretty large map (although bigger in SH than RE) and you had to explore it. Some parts would take puzzles to explore, some others would just take equipment you didn't have yet and that's how they worked - instead of limiting where you could go by only giving you one direction to go in, they gave you a whole map to explore.
That is what this game is, they give you a town like in Silent Hill and you explore it; unlike Silent Hill though, the other things than the main story to do in those towns aren't just a few secrets, but a whole load of side quests with story and lore in themself. They've taken the open world formula from the original (and best) survival horror games and just improved upon it. The scares are in there, the atmosphere is amazing and the gameplay is just reminiscient of everything I love about the genre. They have brought life into this genre, and I thank them. The first Evil Within was more like an homage to the survival horror games like RE4, and this one is more like an homage to the survival horror games that are like Silent Hill 1 and 2. But it isn't just a bad recreation, it is the perfection of the art. They went the extra mile, just using inspiration to get them there.
This game will not be for everyone, but if you liked Alan Wake, Resident Evil, Silent Hill or the first game then you have to play this because you will love it!

The Evil Within 2's story takes place after the events of the first game, and we play as the same main character from the previous game, Sebastian. However, unlike the first game, The Evil Within 2's story seems much more streamlined, understandable and easy to pick up on. In addition, there are plenty of notes/files and side-missions across the game to help better understand the story (and learn more about it). In my opinion, the game improves over its' predecessor in nearly every aspect, from gameplay, which is now much smoother, enemies, level design and more.
The "hub world" in this game is extremely well designed, nearly every house is enterable, and enemies and items have been carefully placed around the world. You can see the interior of each house, regardless of whether it's relevant to the main mission or not, has been carefully crafted. The graphics in this game are also beautiful, they aren't the best, but they definitely are decent, and playing on near-max settings, the environments look extremely detailed.
Moreover, the game is well optimized, and the black bars from the previous game have finally been removed, however, you can turn them on if you'd like to. Sebastian also now has multiple unlockable outfits, there is a shooting range with a bunch of minigames to hone your aiming, a wide variety of new enemy types which are faster than ever, a new pistol and a lot more. Not only that, but the length of the story has drastically been increased as well. I'm only 9-ish hours or so in at the time of writing this review, and I'm only at Chapter 6 (there are 17 chapters in total), bearing in mind I didn't do all the side-missions, and am playing on casual (the medium difficulty, Survival, was already a huge challenge, so the difficulty of this game will no doubt prove challenging to most people).
Overall, I highly recommend anyone who was a fan of the first game, or the survival horror genre to pick this game up, you will love it. To me, The Evil Within 2 is the best third-person survival horror game of 2017, in conjunction with Resident Evil 7 being the best first-person survival horror game of 2017. Pick it up whenever you can, you won't regret it.

Absolutely thrilling experience. This is probably my Game of the Year for 2014. There are a variety of reasons for this which I will explain in this spoiler-free review.
First of all, I will start by saying I am a horror junkie. Ever since Resident Evil I have been addicted to the tension provided by horror games, particularly survival horror, and the puzzle-solving that is often incorporated. Honestly, it is hard to find true survival horror nowadays, as most horror games focus too much on the jump-scare and gore, rather than the actual game.
The best contender in this area before was Amnesia, as it made you hugely vulnerable throughout the story while keeping in touch with the game-play of escaping danger and progressing while managing resources. Dead Space was a disappointment for me because rather than survival it progressively became more and more of an action game throughout the campaign, with jump scares. There is no resource management as you always have ammo. While Dead Space is still excellent, it does not provide true survival horror and instead focuses much more heavily on tension.
Alien: Isolation is not the case. This is by far a survival game at its core. I was genuinely impressed with how the developers chose to create the game. Rather than choosing the obvious course, which would be playing through a space ship infested by multiple xenomorphs (monsters), they chose to add a variety of threats, each one a unique challenge. There is only one xenomorph in the entire game, that follows you throughout your adventure. If you make too much noise, activate electronics, trip over clutter, or otherwise draw attention to yourself, you have a chance of attracting the xenomorpth and if that happens well good ♥♥♥♥ing luck; you will die unless you can truly outsmart it which is unlikely as it has better everything than you. So you constantly need to be careful as you progress and this tension makes you feel like you are actually in danger. I won't spoil the other threats but they are also present, and they are equally as scary. Not just because of their inherent nature, but because if you get caught by them you will summon the Alien.
No other game provides a mechanic like this, and it is truly what makes the game. You have to make decisions. Do you take the quick path and knock over some crates to escape one threat and then attract the Alien? Or do you sneak about and work your way around the threat, or dispatch the threat quietly? Of course this will use up your resources, ammo, and health.
You must manage all your resources which makes the game a true survival horror. Ammunition is highly effective, but precious, and hard to come by. Your health will naturally degrade due to burning fires, broken floors, poisonous gasses, and other threats that you would find on a damaged ship. This makes it imperative to always scrounge around for supplies so you can make health kits and keep yourself going. The inventory also does not pause the game, so you can't pause and quickly heal, you have to do it in a safe place. Again, this only adds to the survival element.
I was somewhat skeptical when I first played this game seeing as how it's based on a film and in my experience very few games actually live up to being a game when they are based on a movie. I♥♥♥♥♥♥you not this game could have nothing to do with Alien and still be a perfect title on its own. The development team did an excellent job to make this a competent undertaking. For example, most games now use mouse smoothing and acceleration (I believe this is done to drive sales for controllers or to make the mouse feel more like a controller, don't ask me I think it's stupid). However, this game, as far as I can tell uses a raw mouse input which feels so much more natural and as a PC gamer works much better than a controller. This game has been polished all around to make it feel complete and well-designed for gamers.
Not only this, but the game focuses heavily on the first film. This was the only good Alien movie in my opinion, excluding the sequel which I regard as a completely different genre than the first. All you need to do is watch the first film and disregard the others, and this game will take you from there. There is no crazy new things that polluted the Alien mythos which I am supremely happy about. In fact, this game is if anything the sequel to the first movie. That is how good it is and that is how high the production value is in this title.
The story is good too, but I won't spoil it. It is enough to keep you interested and is actually refreshing compared to the plot of other similar stories, even though it borrows a few ideas. Again, I was surprised at this. I was expecting a basic rehash of the first Alien movie. Not the case.
In my opinion this is the game Dead Space should have been, and it holds strong as a game of its own. I was completely expecting some high-budget effect-ridden action horror game full of Alien cliches with a terrible story. However, not only did it meet my expectations of what I really wanted in a horror, but it actually exceeds them. Unbelievable.

The Alien AI is fantastic. Many people say it is unpredictable but I disagree - I've found it to be very well implemented to appear random. It uses all of it's senses that you'd expect, making it feel more like a real foe - sight, hearing, smell etc. And it learns from your behavior - I saw it didn't like fire so decided to use the flamethrower to keep it at bay every time it decided to come out. Once it started to realise the fire didn't do very much damage to it and that I didn't pursue it once it retreated, it decided to trick me into thinking it was scared, then circled around and took me down. The best way to describe the AI is it's a simulation. It will be turned on in most of the sections of the game, but not always. The trick is knowing when and where you should be careful - but you should really be careful all the time.
There are issues with some animations, and the gameplay may not be for everyone. As a fan of slow tension building horror and stealth gameplay, I very much enjoyed it.
There have been some complaints that the length of the game is an issue - personally I didn't think so. The last 30min of gameplay are a little bit ridiculous and feel like a broken section of the game that got tacked on in order to have the player end up in a certain area for a cutscene to play out. But this doesn't at all diminish the entire experience.
At the end of the day this won't be a game for everyone... but it is a great achievement non the less.

Broforce is a fun, arcade side scrolling game developed by Free Lives. It was highly sucessful after it's release in 2014. The game is a throwback to action movies from the 1980s, through it's over-the-top action and intense gameplay. The game seems simple in design at first, but after playing for a while, you pick up on the attention to detail that makes this game such a gem.
The controls are simple as well, making it easy to pick up and play. The game runs smoothly and you really feel like a movie hero, slicing and dicing through hoards of no name grunts. As the game goes on, both the game itself and the player made maps (which I'll cover in a moment) add a level of challenge, keeping the game fresh.
As well as the pre-made maps the game comes with, it also has a built in map editor where players can create their own maps to share on the Steam workshop. By being able to share maps, the game maintains a level of mystery. Some maps are made to be played with a somewhat stealthy playstyle by using tunnels and multiple routes and ways to complete maps, whereas others encourage you to go all out, guns blazing, and blow as much stuff up as you can!
In my opinion, the game is best played in co-op. As much fun as it is to run around as MacGyver or Chuck Norris on your own, having a buddy along for the ride just adds to the hilarity that ensues when you play a map or two... or three... five...

The only downside I find to the game was that I just burned myself out. I was having so much fun planting explosives and hip firing that I would just play... and play. The game loses it's appeal after a while. This is not a game you'll sit down and play for hours to level up your character, or build that new house, or go on that raid. This game is purely for the fun aspect. Apart from that there's a total lack of story, but eh. EXPLOSIONS!!!!
Final Ratings:
Graphis: As a throw back to the retro, the graphics breathe life into the old style of game design. They're not next gen, but they're sure as hell prettier :P. Also runs better than next gen.
Gameplay: Broforce is fast paced and over the top. It doesn't have deep game mechanics, but I think we all love a bit of shoot-em-up.
Story: What story?
End result: I give Broforce a solid 7.5 outta teyyan.

Now that patches have sorted out the worst of the issues, I can safely recommend this game.
Pros:
+Emily has an interesting character arc in both high and low chaos, and the arc is different based on said chaos level.
+Karnaca is gorgeous, one of the best looking game settings in recent memory.
+Unlike a certain Fallout 4, the decision to voice the protagonist worked out fine.
+Non lethal is actually fun now instead of frustrating, while still retaining it's unique identity (still gotta be sneaky! Still gotta target individuals and not groups!) and not becoming a copy of lethal that leaves behind sleeping people instead of corpses (cough Mankind Divided cough). The simple fact that if a lone guard spots you and no one is around, you can sock him in the face after parrying sounds like a tiny change, but it fundamentally alters the way you can play the game.
+ Emily has a fantastic power set, for both lethal and non lethal runs. Far Reach might just be my favorite power in any game of 2016. In my opinion her power set upstages Corvos, both in style and in usability.
+ Level design still just as grand as previous entries. Each time I play a level I find something new, some room I haven't been to, or new story tidbits.
+ Unlike the last dishonored, which had fantastic art but muddy textures and jank animations, Dishonored 2 isn't held back by last gen hardware. This is how the first game should have looked.
Cons:
- The rogues gallery isn't quite as compelling as last time. While Jindosh, the Duke, and Delilah are well realised, Breanna, Ramsey, the Crown Killer, and Paolo/Highoverseer leave something to be desired.
- The Dreadful Wale never feels as much like home as the Hound Pits Pub did; with only about three characters on board instead of the colorful cast that was the loyalist conspiracy.
- Corvo's mode should be labelled as an "what if" bonus campaign, because that's what it feels like. While Emily's arc makes sense (she's never fended for herself before. Escaping and regrouping in Karnaca, the place farthest from Gristol, made sense for her) Corvo's less so. No particular reason is given as to why he doesn't turn the boat around after getting his mark back (you learn later it would have been a bad idea to do so, but Corvo had no information at the time to suggest otherwise) and as such the suspension of disbelief suffers a bit since you will constantly ask yourself "Why did he even come to Karnaca?". Still a fun campaign.
- An absolute mess of a launch. Had to be patched several times before it was playable.
- This is a pet peeve of mine but I was hoping for some kind of encore to "Lady Boyle's Last Party" but such an encore never came.
9/10

One of the more memorable features of 1993's Syndicate was lighting people on fire with your flamethrower. The little sprites would run around, arms flailing and screeching in agony until they crumbled into a pile of ash and bone. It was shockingly brutal and so unexpected that it was funny; I'm sure I wasn't the only player who purposely lit civilians on fire just to watch them dash about in their panicked death throes. Apparently the developers of Postal ("Running with Scissors") enjoyed this as much as I did, because they essentially made a game around this trope.
I never played Postal when it was first released in 1996. It was just one of many isometric shooters released around that time - the Crusader games, Gender Wars, SCUD Industrial Revolution, Bedlam - and its only apparent gimmick was that it was purposefully trying to be controversial (and it was successful too, garnering attention from Jack Thompson and the "video-games-are-evil" club). But it didn't seem to stand out in any way beyond that, so it was only until recently that I bought the game.
As it turns out, my initial reactions were correct; this is a shallow game. On its most basic level, the shooting mechanics are acceptable; I point, I shoot, things die. This simplicity, however, is never backed up by anything else; the game lacks in graphics, interesting level design, good sound or music, AI, puzzles... even challenge. It's shooting is about as sophisticated as 1985's "Robotron", except without that seminal's game waves of enemies constantly charging towards you. It's fun for about five minutes, and then boredom quickly sets in. The shock-humor of the game - the aforementioned people on fire, the gut-shot victims crawling about begging for mercy - entertain for another few minutes before that too quickly becomes repetitive. In addition, the levels themselves are fairly short and you can waltz through the core game in a couple of hours (there are bonus levels, but they are just more of the same). It's a tiresome shooter far surpassed by almost any modern games and even most of its contemporaries.

Alright, where do I start?
First off, the short review:
This game is absolutely amazing.
If you like any sort of farming game, such as Harvest Moon and others, then you will love this game.
Alright, onto the longer review:
Slime Rancher is an adorable farming simulator.
In this game, you round up different sorts of slimes and maintain them.
You grow food, (This includes raising chickens for the meat eaters) and
you collect their "Plorts" (Which, I suppose is
and you then sell these plorts for your own financial gain.
You use the money you acquire to buy upgrades to your farm and equipment.
An interesting feature I liked, is that the game has an always changing market.
What do I mean? I mean the value of certain plort types increases and decreases on occasion.
So, it can be /very/ beneficial to hoard up certain plorts and wait for the market to shift into your favor.
The game also has a lot of adventuring to offer, it's fun to run around and explore the
surprisingly massive world, find rare slimes, collect rare foods, and other things.
And the last, and largest part of the game.
IT'S ADORABLE. My god.
I mean, I'm a horror poet and metal-head, and even I had to stop and say
"Awww" more than I'd like to admit. The colors are bright and cheerful,
and the game doesn't fail to increase your mood. It's a great time-killer,
and an amazing antidepressant. And, there's not much else to say.
I hope my review was helpful to someone.
Thank you for your time.

For a short game, literally got all 3 endings in about 6 hours, it was absolutely gorgeous. It was by far one of the best, actually the best, RPG Maker game I've played so far. I will put specifics below.
Story: One of the three biggest things that made this short game amazing and memorable. The story of the main character risking her life to save her older sister is maybe a cliche to an extent, but they got that cliche and made it beautiful. The story has 3 endings total, each one being emotional and memorable. This is one of those select few were I actually loved all the alternate endings. Personally speaking though, the 3rd ending is the best.  8/10 for the story (could easily be 10 if it wasn't only 6hrs long)
Graphics: The second biggest thing that made me love this game. Anyone who played Visual Novels willl more than likely see what I mean when I say these graphics are absolutely amazing. This game has some of the best graphics I've ever seen in RPG Maker games, competing with a lot of Visual Novels. Of course, the gameplay graphic is mediocre, but you can't expect much from RPG Maker in that aspect. (Still amazing for being made in RPG Maker). It's the story images that hit me hard. They were the biggest thing that made me love this game. 9/10 for the graphics
Music: This is definetly important in games. What background to play at what time? Should it be silent? Loud or quite? Fast or slow? Well, this game did an amazing job with the soundtrack. I am using the piano theme on my phone for a ringtone as I type this, and I am loving it. The soundtrack was beautifuly done, adding a lot of emotion to the story and images. 9/10 (the music was beautiful, but a few played several times throughout making it not quite a 10)
Gameplay: The gameplay was interesting in several ways. The creator got rid of the turn-base combat and instead implemented his own. You move around freely and attack enemies by running into them. You also us the buttons 'Q'W'E'R" to use your skills. It sounds sort of simple, which it is, but the enemies make it challenging. Especially the bosses, who have unique skills of their own and can do AOEs causing major damage. I've died by all the main bosses except 2, the first boss (Slime) and the semi-final boss (Final if you get Ending 1). 7.5/10 (feel like more could be added)
Overall, I give the game a 8.5/10. It had a great story combined with both great graphics and music. The controls were simple, yet amazing in their own way. I would most definitely reccomend this FREE game to anyone who loves RPGs and Visual Novels. I would've proudly paid for it if it costed money. =(^,.,^)=

When i finally got around to playing the first Evil Within about a year ago i was very impressed by that game, especially considering all the problems it had at launch, and when i completed it i couldn't wait for a sequel. I didn't find out about this game until two days before release while i was replaying the first one and was very surprised.
My first thought was that surely they are going to ruin the sequel, remove everything that was good from the first, fill it with microtransaction and the pc release would be made with the least amount of effort possible to make it "run", but i decided to give it a chance and look and behold: A pc friendly game without any microtransactions.
Just because you enjoyed the first game that's no guarantee you will like this, it's not just more of the same. Rather than a linear game with levels designed to be played in order you have a fairly open world. As soon as you complete the tutorial part of the game you are free to go anywhere you want in the first area, whether you want to just get on with the main mission or if you want to go scavenge some ammunition.
Progression with the main missions is required to unlock further areas so it's not truly open world.
The story is nothing special and is quite boring and predictable and will make no sense if you haven't played the first game but it ties up most of the loose strings from the first game.
The general enemy design is mostly the same, general zombie like enemies with the occasional deliciously macabre enemy or boss.
Most of the gameplay is largely unchanged. The basic enemies are nearly identical to those from the first game and there's a boss fight trown in here and there. You have much of the same weapons including the agony crossbow wich is now named warden crossbow for some reason. You can still sneak up behind enemies and kill them with a sneak attack or you can just shoot them until they're dead. You can also still throw bottles into the enmies head to stun them and allow you to stealth kill them, although it's more difficult to do now.
Green gel is now mostly found from killed enemies rather than found lying around and is used to unlock and upgrade various abilites such as increasing max health, reducing weapon sway or letting you move faster when crouched.
Weapon parts, wich can be found lying around, is now used to upgrade weapons and bolts at workbenches and ammo pouches can be found in various places to allow you to carry more ammo of a certain type.
There is also a crafting system where you can find things such as plants to make medicine or gunpowder to make ammo.
Crafting anything but medicine costs more resources if done in the field rather than at a workbench making you consider if you should use that gunpowder now to make some bullets or save it to make more later.
Ammo management is still a very important thing, especially at the beginning of the game where you really feel the pain of each miss or even just getting a bodyshot instead of a headshot.
On a more pc specific note i have to say that this is a good port. There's settings for turning on/off motion blur, depth of field and bloom for those who hate that (i do). You can select a fov from 45 to 90. There's a generous mouse speed setting meaning you probably won't think it's too fast at the lowest setting (or the other way around) and no mouse acceleration or other mouse issues apart from a slighly floaty mouse in the menus.
There's settings for sprinting and taking cover to be hold or toggle, a lot of hud options, and there's also a setting to enable the letterboxing from the first game (the horror!) with a joke in the description showing they realise it was a big mistake to make it forced in the first game and that they also have some humour (there's another joke about it when you beat the game and unlock it).
A surprisingly well made pc port wich i have only a few gripes with: no console (yet) and it could have had more graphics options. In fact there's not really any real graphics options like textures, effects, particles etc.. so if you don't have a good computer you're out of luck.
One thing i found very annoying was what i can only call a graphical glitch wich i guess stems from the rendering method they use. It's the same one that alien isolation had where there is a lot of odd aliasing and shimmering where there really shouldn't be any and the in game anti aliasing (fxaa, taa or both) barely has any effect on it while making everything blurry.
I finished the game on survival(normal) in about 15 hours but i'm already looking forward to replaying it on nightmare(hard). There's also classic mode when you've beaten the game once: No autosaves, limited manual saves and no upgrades (neither weapons nor abilites).
I encountered only a single bug where i went into a room, acivated an event, some things happened(no spoilers) and when it was over i couldn't open a container inside. But there was an autosave from about 2 minutes before that i reloaded.
This time i opened the container before triggering the event and everything worked as it sould.
All in all a good game, but lacking the feeling of the first. More a twisted lovechild of several other games and franchises including Resident Evil(there's several clear homages to RE4), Silent Hill, Zombiu, the latest Tomb Raiders and a few others.

Honestly, probably my favorite game of 2015 and will stay that way for a while. People always complain about the performance and the story and that its repetitive and boring. So here's a serious review, talking about the aspect that
actually matter in a video game. Lets get started:
Graphics: Looks amazing. Nothing else to say. If you say this game doesnt look fantastic you either have a toaster as a PC (in which case you shouldnt have even bought it to begin with, but we'll talk about that later) or you just cant tell between a good graphics game and a bad one. The explosions make me feel like Im in the game, and Im the one CAUSING them. Its honestly one of the most amazing experiences I have had with a video game.
Performance: So this is the main complain about the game. I dont know how it is on AMD (heard its crap tho) so I'll only talk about how it is for me. My build is a GTX 950 with an I5-4460 core (we will ignore other stats for now, as they dont matter as much). At first, I was worried I wouldnt be able to run it at all after seeing my build is under the minimum, and yes, on the first run I had 30 FPS while just playing and 15FPS while explosions were happening. So obviously, that was CRAP. No one likes to play a game on♥♥♥♥♥♥FPS. Even on the lowest graphics I had 40FPS, no more. But then, I messed with the settings and wasn't surprised to find that the V-Sync (Vertical Sync in the graphics settings) in this game absolutely DEMOLISHES the FPS. After turning V-Sync off, I'm now able to play with most setting on High and overall high graphics, and enjoy 60FPS with or without explosions. OK. This is how this review will go. First I will state my general thought of Just Cause 3, then I will list pros and cons, then i will dive much further into detail and then finally say some things I think should have been in the game.
First if all, I adore Just Cause 3, it is easily the best game of 2015 for me. (I haven't played the Witcher 3 yet though.)
PROS:
- Beautiful, and huge map.
- Great aesthetics.
- Better storyline than Just Cause 2.
- Trains :D
- Great choice of vehicles.
- Driving is pretty damn great.
- Etc...
CONS:
- Lots of the map is empty terrain.
- No multiplayer (Mod coming soon :D)
- Storyline is not as good as it could be (it is a just cause game though.)
- After you 100% complete the game, there is not much more to do.
Now, I will go into much more detail about these factors.
THE MAP:
Medici is a beautiful mediterranean paradise filled with things to see and do. Unfortunately, many parts of the map are under devoloped, like Insula Striate, which is the largest island, has few cities and towns besides the southern coastline and has lots of empty space. I think Avalanche could've taken the time to fill Insula Striate with many more towns and cites, in the mountains and on the northern coast. I also think they should've added more islands to the south west part of the ocean as well. I'll give the map a 7/10
AESTHETICS AND GRAPHICS:
Just Cause 3 may not have as good graphics as some of the other releases this year, *cough* EA Battlefront *cough* but I really think that the game looks great and handles pretty damn good on my PC (Specs listed at the bottom of the review). The light and colourful aesthetic along with the cheery music really makes a mediterrean island that works. Aesthetics: 10/10 Graphics 8.5/10
STORYLINE:
Just Cause 3 has a much better storyline than Just Cause 2, with characters you care about and laugh about, and some really fun missions. (I won't go into to much detail because I don't want to spoil the plot.) It may not be on the story telling calibar of a Telltale game or a Netflix original series, but it is damn good for a game about flying around in a squirrel suit blowing up bridges.  7/10
VEHICLES:
Just Cause 3 offers a great variety of vehicles from F1 race cars to cargo planes. The cargo plane and the transport boat are really cool because they can hold vehicles, which will allow for all out wars to happen in multiplayer, or you could just reanact the plane scene from Furious 7. One thing I think they missed out on was enabling the semi truck to pull trailers, you could fill with people or vehicles, for use with the rebels in singleplayer or with your friends in multiplayer. Also the Urga Fura's description says it can fit 12 people but it cant. :(      And this time around, unlike Just Cause 2, the vehicles dont look like crumpled paper when they are damaged. Trains are cool but I think they should be longer, faster and maybe have different types, like military transport, passenger trains, and rebel trains. All the cars handle great and drifting works fine, all in all a 8.5/10
POST-COMPLETION:
This section will almost be redundent after the multiplayer comes out, but Just Cause 3, has no post-game what so ever. And by this I mean post-100%, not post-story. After post-story, you still have to take over the rest of the map, which by the way I recommend not rushing to take over everything or else the game will get quite boring because there will be almost no military, and find all the collectibles to unlock everything. But after you have done all these things, the game becomes very boring because there is nothing to do. In the mean time I have replayed the game to the point where I have beat the story and used mods to get everything in the game, but I've left most of the map military-controlled. Until multiplayer comes out there is not much we can do about this. Post-game/story: 5/10
At this point if I averaged out all the scores, the game would get a measly 7.2/10 which is actually better than most reviewers gave it.
But heres the thing, lots of those review companies didn't really play the game to its most potential, the memories I will have of being slingshotted across the map inside my jeep because of a glitchy train, or seeing a jet randomly come flying out of the ground, or the first time I drove the F1 car, or laughing at Mario's lines, make up for some of the flaws. For just all around fun i give the game a solid 10/10, but heres the thing. That would still give the game a 7.6/10 which I do not believe is accurate. So ♥♥♥♥ THE MATH.
I give Just Cause 3 an 8.8/10 and with some of the approvements I have suggested it could easily be a 9.5/10.
I recommend Just Cause 3 with every cell in my brain. Game of the ♥♥♥♥ing year.
TL:DR Great game, slightly empty map, good cars, 8.8/10.
EDIT: David Tennant voices himself, as a kidnapped radio host. 10/10
EDIT ALMOST A YEAR LATER: The DLC's have improved the game further, making the map less empty, and adding more content. It runs better than it used to, but, after playing the Witcher 3, it is now my second favorite game from 2015, cause the Witcher is just so damn good. Nano's Multiplayer will be out soon :) I also take back my statement about it having good driving, the driving feels weird and heavy, but i also feel its better than the previous game.

After 60+ hours I think I can say the game is okay. If you are hoping for the next big thing in open world gameplay, look elsewhere. This game is about as cookie cutter as it gets. The only new features are big explosions (and boy are they pretty) the improved tethers and the new wingsuit (whee!). The huge map feels a little empty at times and it hardly looks like there's a war or violent revolution going on. The story missions are okay. Freeing towns gets a bit boring after a while, with very little variation or challenge. Some of the basic abilities are locked away and you need to earn them doing challenges dotted all over the map. The first few for the wingsuit and the grappling hook are essential to get, but I couldn't be bothered to unlock them all. I had more fun doing crazy stunts or making up my own silly stuff to do.
If you look at the large number of complaints in the reviews you can see there are quite a few bugs. I've seen a few of them myself, though not all the time. These included flashing terrain patches, falling through the map (usually while driving off-road), physics going crazy and the occasional crash to the desktop. Control prompts are also often for the wrong input device. Still haven't found that space bar on my controller. ;) The online challenge thing is also broken half the time. Don't bother with that.
I played this game on an i7-6820HK with 16GB RAM and a GeForce GTX 980M at a resolution of 1920x1080. Performance seemed fine to me with all the settings maxed out.
So in summary this is a tentative yes. Just Cause 3 is not great, but not terrible. If you're on the fence, wait for a sale or a permanent price drop. Also compare your hardware specs with the people complaining on the forums and in the reviews.

Well the first chapter was a fun ride.
I've never played any of the previous King's Quest games so I went into this nearly blind, with the exception for a bit of the Game Grumps playthrough. Boy am I glad I picked this game up.
From the moment the elder King Graham starts making his puns he set the tone of the game; adventerous with bits of comedy here and there. This game isn't quite a point and click adventure, since you actually control Graham with the WASD or control stick, but the basics of the game would fall into that category. Find an object, find an object for previous object to interact with, gain new items or a new path, and repeat. There are a few "action sequences" peppered in, but for the most part you'll be exploring the environment looking for ways to advance.
This game is heavily story driven, and the actions you make subtly affect the way the game plays out. For example, will you leave a tip for a store, or just take the item out? While the game may be light gameplay-wise, it makes up for it with an enjoyable cast of characters, from the horribly inept Knights of Daventry to the traveling Merchant who cherishes his  pet "unicorns".
Still, this game is more for the problem solver and, as mentioned before, the majority of the game will be spent traveling between many points. In other words, this is a slower paced game than others. If you're expecting to go into this game swords drawn, you'll be sorely disappointed. If, however, you're looking for a game that'll tug at your heart strings a little, this will be worth the check.
At the moment of this review, there is only one chapter out, with the other four to be released later. You can buy them 1 chapter at a time, as a whole season pass, or buy the complete collection, which is the same as the season pass but with a playable epilogue.
Overall I'd highly recommend this game. Sure the gameplay is very slow-paced compared to other games, but it more than makes up for it with the clever puzzles and the witty dialogue. If you're looking for a good story, this game is for you.

Absolutely thrilling experience. This is probably my Game of the Year for 2014. There are a variety of reasons for this which I will explain in this spoiler-free review.
First of all, I will start by saying I am a horror junkie. Ever since Resident Evil I have been addicted to the tension provided by horror games, particularly survival horror, and the puzzle-solving that is often incorporated. Honestly, it is hard to find true survival horror nowadays, as most horror games focus too much on the jump-scare and gore, rather than the actual game.
The best contender in this area before was Amnesia, as it made you hugely vulnerable throughout the story while keeping in touch with the game-play of escaping danger and progressing while managing resources. Dead Space was a disappointment for me because rather than survival it progressively became more and more of an action game throughout the campaign, with jump scares. There is no resource management as you always have ammo. While Dead Space is still excellent, it does not provide true survival horror and instead focuses much more heavily on tension.
Alien: Isolation is not the case. This is by far a survival game at its core. I was genuinely impressed with how the developers chose to create the game. Rather than choosing the obvious course, which would be playing through a space ship infested by multiple xenomorphs (monsters), they chose to add a variety of threats, each one a unique challenge. There is only one xenomorph in the entire game, that follows you throughout your adventure. If you make too much noise, activate electronics, trip over clutter, or otherwise draw attention to yourself, you have a chance of attracting the xenomorpth and if that happens well good ♥♥♥♥ing luck; you will die unless you can truly outsmart it which is unlikely as it has better everything than you. So you constantly need to be careful as you progress and this tension makes you feel like you are actually in danger. I won't spoil the other threats but they are also present, and they are equally as scary. Not just because of their inherent nature, but because if you get caught by them you will summon the Alien.
No other game provides a mechanic like this, and it is truly what makes the game. You have to make decisions. Do you take the quick path and knock over some crates to escape one threat and then attract the Alien? Or do you sneak about and work your way around the threat, or dispatch the threat quietly? Of course this will use up your resources, ammo, and health.
You must manage all your resources which makes the game a true survival horror. Ammunition is highly effective, but precious, and hard to come by. Your health will naturally degrade due to burning fires, broken floors, poisonous gasses, and other threats that you would find on a damaged ship. This makes it imperative to always scrounge around for supplies so you can make health kits and keep yourself going. The inventory also does not pause the game, so you can't pause and quickly heal, you have to do it in a safe place. Again, this only adds to the survival element.
I was somewhat skeptical when I first played this game seeing as how it's based on a film and in my experience very few games actually live up to being a game when they are based on a movie. I♥♥♥♥♥♥you not this game could have nothing to do with Alien and still be a perfect title on its own. The development team did an excellent job to make this a competent undertaking. For example, most games now use mouse smoothing and acceleration (I believe this is done to drive sales for controllers or to make the mouse feel more like a controller, don't ask me I think it's stupid). However, this game, as far as I can tell uses a raw mouse input which feels so much more natural and as a PC gamer works much better than a controller. This game has been polished all around to make it feel complete and well-designed for gamers.
Not only this, but the game focuses heavily on the first film. This was the only good Alien movie in my opinion, excluding the sequel which I regard as a completely different genre than the first. All you need to do is watch the first film and disregard the others, and this game will take you from there. There is no crazy new things that polluted the Alien mythos which I am supremely happy about. In fact, this game is if anything the sequel to the first movie. That is how good it is and that is how high the production value is in this title.
The story is good too, but I won't spoil it. It is enough to keep you interested and is actually refreshing compared to the plot of other similar stories, even though it borrows a few ideas. Again, I was surprised at this. I was expecting a basic rehash of the first Alien movie. Not the case.
In my opinion this is the game Dead Space should have been, and it holds strong as a game of its own. I was completely expecting some high-budget effect-ridden action horror game full of Alien cliches with a terrible story. However, not only did it meet my expectations of what I really wanted in a horror, but it actually exceeds them. Unbelievable.

The Alien AI is fantastic. Many people say it is unpredictable but I disagree - I've found it to be very well implemented to appear random. It uses all of it's senses that you'd expect, making it feel more like a real foe - sight, hearing, smell etc. And it learns from your behavior - I saw it didn't like fire so decided to use the flamethrower to keep it at bay every time it decided to come out. Once it started to realise the fire didn't do very much damage to it and that I didn't pursue it once it retreated, it decided to trick me into thinking it was scared, then circled around and took me down. The best way to describe the AI is it's a simulation. It will be turned on in most of the sections of the game, but not always. The trick is knowing when and where you should be careful - but you should really be careful all the time.
There are issues with some animations, and the gameplay may not be for everyone. As a fan of slow tension building horror and stealth gameplay, I very much enjoyed it.
There have been some complaints that the length of the game is an issue - personally I didn't think so. The last 30min of gameplay are a little bit ridiculous and feel like a broken section of the game that got tacked on in order to have the player end up in a certain area for a cutscene to play out. But this doesn't at all diminish the entire experience.
At the end of the day this won't be a game for everyone... but it is a great achievement non the less.

With the release of Rome Total 2 - Emperor Edition, I think it's fairly safe to say the game is finally finished. After a rather dismal start the developers have been pushing the patches through, addressing the major problems of the game, such as siege AI and diplomacy (fixed in the latest patch), that made the game difficult to enjoy.
As someone who jumped straight from Rome 1/Medieval Total War because sadly, I had an old imac for about six years straight into Rome 2, I was baffled to say the least. However once I got used to the interface, food/public order and the diplomacy, I had a fantastic time. The game looks and sounds wonderful (Though I did get the Rome 1 Soundtrack mod) from it's dynamic cities to watching your men hack down the enemy in bloody fashion. The province system is cool as it makes you feel that you really have to fight to secure lands and play it smart when it comes to building and recruiting. The combat has been improved even further in this patch by slowing down the fights thus making casualties more frequent and taking the risk of going into battle on the open field an actual concern much like it was in real life.
Also, if you have an issue with any aspect of the game, you can probably find a mod for it made by a very active modding community. Personally I am a huge advocat of mod support for games.
Anyway, while this review wasn't the most detailed, I do reccomend you try the game if you haven't played it yet and/or returning to the series. I do feel it's a great game in a genre that I think should require some more attention because hey, who doesn't want to be the next Caesar (without the whole assasination thing of course)?

I have mixed feelings about this game. FIrstoff, although I haven't completed the game, I can see how intricate and innovative the RPG elements incorporated into the game are, and clearly contribute to the quality of the gameplay. Moreover, the plotline is intense and developed, and is clearly more than just an excuse plot, as many games in its time period would use. The graphics, while they seem rather dissappointing by modern standards, are stunning considering the game's release in the 90's. The atmosphere is perfect, the music is adrenaline-inducing, and the objective-based gameplay is perfect. Yet still, I found myself unable to progress past a certain point in this game. I can't quite pinpoint what exactly it was. Perhaps it was a mixture of the numb fear this game managed to invoke in me, despite its underdeveloped graphics, and the frustration I had with the lack of guidance the game gives you in terms of your stat builds and ability progression, Spending your cybernetic modules wisely is crucial, and blowing them trying to become well rounded in your build will generally screw you over, as you won't have the level of a certain ability required to perform certain tasks to progress through the game. I also felt overwhelmed with the amount of pressure put on me by the game, by the enemies, by the time limits sometimes impressed on me, and by the choices I had to make regarding my stat and ability choices. Between all of these things, it was difficult for me to pull through and finish this game. I will probably revisit it later, but for now, it's gonna be sitting in my steam library for a while

Screenshots can't express how fun and addictive System Shock 2 is to play. You're hoarding ammo and sneaking around corners while mutants murmur terrifying things into your headshet. "WE SEEK," they announce, letting you know that as soon as they find you, you're mutant chow. You check your inventory for the ammo that will perfectly take down the mutants, but then a cyborg rounds the corner, ganking you with throwing stars like a ninja.
Although I'm way late to the party on this game, I was pleased to see that many of the mechanics I love in modern games are present in System Shock 2. There's the shooter/rpg hybrid gameplay that I enjoy in Bioshock and Borderlands. There's also the difficulty level and tension of Resident Evil 4, right down to the limited inventory space. Graphically, it seems dated in comparison to even Half-Life, but the games share a fear factor, causing the player to constantly quick save for fear of being brutally taken down by some random foe around the corner.
In a way, the game is teaching you to play it like a classic Mega Man game. You learn where to predict enemy spawns and which weapons are best for taking them down. I came into the rpg elements having no clue as to what skills would help my character, but as I progressed I learned by trial and error. It's one of those games where dying makes you excited to get better, rather than rage quitting altogether.
I recommend this game to anyone who likes the original Half-Life or Bioshock. It's the kind of game that I never expected to love, but it ended up really surprising me.

I really like this game and the co-op part, but what ruins it is not having a difficulty setting.  It wouldn't be that hard to add one and just give the player extra health at the start of each map if they pick easy setting for the map.
Your only option for trying to make it through each map is to die 5-10 times and memorize where the enemies are on that map.  Also, part of the problem is you can't see some of the enemies on screen, but they can shoot you dead.  So you pretty much have to charge in and die to get an idea of who's there and where they're standing.  Having to charge around each map and memorize it 5-10 times gets really boring for a group of guys who just want to have some fun after a long day at work.  And even if you get the guys to memorize it, you still have to get lucky and not all get killed, because it's really easy to get killed.  Since they reworked the whole game, you think a difficulty setting would be easy enough to add.  This would also help replayability I think, because you could take on a harder level once you beat each one.
Cheat codes don't let you progress if you use them, so that's not an answer.  I'm disappointed that they didn't take that one easy, extra step to make it fun for everyone.

SUMMARY
I can recommend Dishonored 2 and I have to admit I have enjoyed it. The gameplay is pretty smooth, each location of the game is very different and they all look beautiful and atmospehere made by decent sounds and lore is almost perfect. However the PC optimalization is very poor, the framerate is truly unstable and in some locations the game tends to crash. 90/100
PROS
- each location is different and the game often shows you new stuff or lets you observe little beautiful details
- the gameplay feels good, it is based on the 1st Dishonored but it adds new stuff as well
- the sounds are pretty much perfect, the atmosphere is well done
- I liked the soundtrack, it has few very well composed tracks and some decent tracks that make the feel of the game complete
- the non-lethal way is interesting and fun to play
- the characters were written almost excellently in the typical style of Dishonored
CONS

- the story could have been more inovative and the game could have felt a bit more story based

The story in itself was better in the first Dishonored, but the quality of writing and dialog was just as good in this one. After few of the patches the game started to run pretty much fine, had very little problems. Also the game seems to be pretty well polished gameplay-wise, with close to no gameplay bugs during the 20 hour playthrough.
The level design is awesome. Basicly in all the levels and chapters upon reaching the goal or objective I had figured out several ways I could've reached the end. It was awesome to realise at the end of the level that I could've got there so many different ways. The game also asks you in the beginning if you want to play without the superpowers, making this as close to Thief sequel as you can get. This also means that the levels are designed in a way that you can reach the end at least through one route that doesn't require teleporting on anything like that.
Game was challenging enough too. I played on Hard and tried to be as stealthy as possible (I think in the end I killed total of 3 enemies, of which one was an accident where I threw a dude down the elevator shaft and realised he died when I got the stats for the level...) and there were many times when I really had to think how I will get through the level without killing anyone (or get detected).
All in all Dishonored 2 is as great a sequel as you can hope for. Once most of the technical stuff was fixed the game ran pretty well, looked great and felt awesome. I wouldn't say the story was a dissappointment, but it felt a bit lackluster compared to the original.

This game is much more fun than I expected it to be. I literally only picked it up because it was free, and because I thought it was a VN (I didn't read the description when I got it). I didn't get round to playing it for ages, and I regret this fact.
The game is super simple and easy to play. This isn't really a bad thing, it feels like a casual game with a story, so you need to play expecting and understanding that. I've only tried the default difficulty, and picked normal difficulty on all the bosses as well. There is an easy option, which I haven't tried, because it's really unnecessary. To give an example: I didn't realise that you could upgrade your skills, even though it should have been really obvious. I completed the game without it, and only realised I could when I went for another ending when I pressed the wrong button and brought up the screen. I'll mention this again later because it caused a bug I want to warn about.
The game is really short. It took me a bit over 6 hours to complete, get every chest, do every side quest (the chest, slime and sheep), create all the armour and weapons, (including the special weapon and armour), and see all three endings. Admittedly, the ending wasn't a complete play through. I got ending one first, which gave a hint to the next ending, which I then did which gave you a choice, which was obviously the next two endings. If you're one of those that don't like playing multiple times to get all the endings you don't have to worry, you can save and just do the last bit three times.
Finding some of the chests were awkward, strangely it was the first chests that caused me to struggle, I didn't realise you could cross the river with Q for ages!
Most were pretty easy to get, the best bet in games like this is simply getting to the end of the dungeon, then going back to the beginning, because you usually have a new skill that lets you get some you couldn't before.
The boss fights were fun, but too easy. It's not really a big problem for this kind of game, if they were too hard it would break the flow of the story, but at the minute you can take them all on and win first try. An option for harder difficulties would be nice. Admittedly I haven't done a second play through, and I can't remember if there was a choice in difficulty at the start.
It isn't clear enough that you can't return to previous dungeons, or if it is I completely missed it. Part of my playtime was actually playing again from the start after completing half the second dungeon, because I didn't work out that you could cross the river with Q for a while and thought that you got a boat or something further on in the game.
The biggest fault I had with this game were the king bosses. They are optional, they just drop a stone to make the legendary equipment for that dungeon, but they are not difficult to kill. The sign says to try it when you have elite armour, but you could remove all your armour and take them on, though it would take ages doing so. The reason is, is because they have absolutely no combat skills or movement. When you attack them, they get pushed back, and deal you reflection damage like all other monsters, but they don't actually attack you or move. This means you can simply stand there and wait for your health to regen, or you wait for your mana to regen and use Q to avoid the reflection damage. It takes a while without using elite equipment, but far from impossible. Getting legendary gear usually should feel like an achievement won after lots of hard work, but right now it's simply an award for your patience. Not only that, but once you've got the set, every monster other than bosses just does only 1 damage to you, so you heal quicker than you take damage, and everything dies in one hit.
The puzzles are simple, the only one that took any amount of time was the last one with the gems, but that was simply trial and error as the thing told you how many are right, so you just had to do one gem at a time until you got it.
There are two options for codes. The first gives you materials at the start of each dungeon (they are grindable, so you don't have to do it), which you get by visiting there Facebook page. The page didn't come up for me, probably because it's a Japanese page, so it took some digging. Here it is for your convenience:
You don't have to like the page for the code, it's in the about page which I've put the link for, but if you've got to the point where you need it then you've already started playing an awesome game that was provided for free, so don't be a scumbag and like the page.
There's another code, which is for the bonus room, which you get by filling out a questionnaire at the end (Did you like the game, etc.). I'll provide the link, but complete the game first, otherwise it's spoilers. I won't give the code, the developer worked hard on the game and deserves a little feedback.
goo gl Lav2RV (put a period(.) in the first pace, and a forward slash(/) in the second, it get's removed it I paste the url).
This is the url used in the game, I've not expanded it since the developer might be using it for basic statistic purposes.
There was only one bug that I came across in this game. When fighting the last boss again for the second ending, I missed placed my fingers and pressed a few of the top row of keys trying to find the right one, and whatever I pressed caused the skill page to open. While on the skill page, I was still being attacked, but it was at the start of the fight so I didn't mind dying and thought I'd just quickly see how far I could upgrade the skills with an entire games worth of points (If your curious, I could upgrade my q skill to 41.)
I died while this screen was still up, which caused the sp cost numbers of the skills to remain on the screen, even when loading in a new game. It went after closing an opening the game again, but that's still a pain you probably want to avoid, so make sure you're out of a fight when upgrading them.
Lastly, I just wanted to mention something about the game that might put people off, and why it shouldn't. This game is made in RPGMaker, as you can see in the tags. This tag doesn't even really need to be there, because the developer's pretty much developed the game himself, the combat system and boss battles are completely unique, it's not the turn based boring crap that RPGmaker does by default. It's got its own beautiful artwork and sprites, dialogue boxes and menus as well. If he had charged money for it, I would have bought it.

Few times in my life have I been caught so completely off gaurd by such an innocent little game. As one who loves the concept of free, Eternal Senia popped up in my Steam Queue and appealed to my long untouched love of Ys at the cost of absolutely nothing. RPG maker games tend to be a warning sign, but the overwhelming praise convinced me, and I'm glad it did.
In just one day--Christmas day I might add--I dumped 10 hours into this little gem, seeing all the endings and collecting every secret in every nook and cranny. I haven't done that with any game in ages, but there was something so simply...enthralling about Eternal Senia. Most impressively, for an RPG maker game, Holy Priest bent the engine to his own will and developed an impressive real time battle system, which from all that I've experienced is completely unheard of. With no breaks to the flow of the game, I found myself being drawn into the otherwise middle of the road story like I hadn't been in ages. It scratched an itch I didn't even know I had, and I suddenly found myself spending a lot less time with my family then I intended. Kinda feel guilty about that one.
There was something about the clunky localization that kept the story from ever really engaging me emotionally, but something definitely worked because I didn't put the darn thing down til I hit the credits. The pacing of the tale, told in three acts, was one I found fairly engaging, but the amount of content here alone is staggering; dozens of secrets, multiple bosses both required and optional, a crafting system, and an entirely seperate procedurally generated set of dungeons populate the entire landscape. The main bosses even have multiple difficulties prompted before the fight, which I have to respect. The crafting system makes it rather easy to get yourself well overpowered, but tackling a main boss' hard mode garuntees no matter your gear will be a tough fight. To say the least, the balancing is extremely impressive. The art surrounding the couple of cutscenes and the boss sprites always impressed, and the demand for comprehending patterns and callsigns on a variety of enemies big and small genuinely made me smile; there is passion in this game. A lot of it.
Good god I wish I could give this game some of my money. I feel guiltier about that than I do about the christmas thing. There are garbage RPG maker games littering steam right now asking for 5, 10, 15 dollars, and this wonderful piece of interactive wonder is free, and I find that a crime of so many levels. There's even a hidden developer's commentary breaking down how he made the game and the stuff he learned along the way. What's not to love? Since I can't give it money, I'll give it my support: download this great game.
I really would love to see what these guys would be capable of doing with a budget, that's for sure. Guess I'm a fan now.

You might think that the central mechanic of walking your character into monsters makes the game boring.
Ironically, that isn't really the problem.
If you have ever played any of the Ys games, this is fundamentally a dumbed-down version of those games with much less dynamic moment-to-moment gameplay.
On top of that, the game was originally written in Japanese, then translated into English... and while the translation is never non-sensical, it is obvious that it was not translated by a native speaker.
But even beyond that... the story just isn't very interesting at all. You're a girl who has lost her sister. You need to go find her. You run into... some people along the way. None of them are very interesting or memorable, nor is the protagonist, for that matter. There is just nothing gripping about the story of this game.
Given the very simplistic, not very rewarding gameplay and the unrewarding story, there is just no reason to play this game. It isn't terrible, but lots of things aren't terrible; for something to be worth your time, it should be actively good.
This is not.
Your time is better spent doing other things. Read a book instead; it will be much more fulfilling. Or play a better game.

Just Cause 3 is definitely one of the best feeling open world games that has come out in recent years, and I really think thats saying something.
About five or so years ago when Just Cause 2 released it got less than stellar reviews, but the general consensus was that it was a great summer blockbuster fill in game to hold you off until the fall season of games come out. Back then that was all Just Cause was to people, and the past few years have been good to Avalanche Studios.
They've released Mad Max as a standalone game, with a likely franchise to come in the future which leaves their cash cow (Just Cause) to experiment and change up.
On that note, there's virtually nothing that changes about how terrible the vehicular handling has been. As it was in previous games, I wish to god they didn't focus at all on driving. You would think after four years driving would be improved, even tweaked a bit, especially with Mad Max under their belt. Here it feels like it was deliberately scrapped and something else slightly worse was replaced with it. Same thing can be said for flying and riding bikes. The upshot? You can pull unrealistic maneauvers and nitrous boosts in virtually any vehicle, which makes up for the terrible mobility.
Its like they knew it was terrible but didn't change it because they either didn't have time or didnt have money to bother with revamping the driving mechanics. I feel like all of the focus in Just Cause 3 was focused on ironing out the wing suit.  More on that in a bit.
Vehicles suck. They handle worse than poorly and I advise staying away if you really wanna enjoy the game.
Combat is far more improved in Just Cause 2. Not at all varied, but the reaction times of NPCs is much smoother and character animations adds for more immersive kills and takedowns. You'll be spending most of your time in the air though so I wouldn't worry about how they look. When the♥♥♥♥♥♥hits the fan enemies don't stop spawning until the base is captured, which keeps the pace up. While they aren't too complicated to beat I wish that the enemies had a bit more acrobatic ability than what they have.  Harnesses and rope darts would be great additions to make them worth♥♥♥♥♥♥against me.
They never are, and I feel like every time I go up against another barrage of choppers or a herd of tanks my suspension to disbelief in the fight is shrinking. I kick♥♥♥♥♥ The trick is to do it flawlessly.
The weapons aren't as varied as you would hope but there are plenty and trust in me they got plenty of stopping power.
The greatest addition to Just Cause 3 is without a doubt the wing suit. In previous games Rico has amassed a reputation as a daredevil with lots of useful gadgets, but we could never hold him in the same light as Batman or the Green Arrow. If he isn't a super hero in your eyes now, then your blind. Indeed the Scorpion's grapple hook/wing suit combo give him the ability to fly indefinitely and with some impressive maneuvers. I don't even touch vehicles anymore because of how easier and quicker it is to fly there. The controls of flying are a bit difficult but super addicting once you get the hang of it.
I would spend $44.99 again just for the wing suit.
A bittersweet design choice is locking upgrades and perks behind obnoxious challenges and game activities. Some of these are fun, tasking you with flying and blowing♥♥♥♥♥♥up. Above all th epoint is to get you to really pay attention to the detail of the game before you get cool upgrades, I'm okay with this, but it shows how terrible certain mechanics are IE: Driving, etc.
They got us to play the game to get the perks we wanted, but is a frustrated customer what they really wanted?
The game runs like butter for me and I'm rocking a gtx970 with an i7-3770 ivy bridge. I know that performance was stunted in the earlier days of release because of how the online leaderboards kept signing people out.  There has been some debate and contraversy about the online mechanics in the game having you sign in (LOL its a single player game). It seems silly at first but considering how many players there are per day playing the game and how quickly and often they are trying to break each others record, the leaderboards are an awesome awesome addition. Basically, everytime you get in game other players have beaten your record or set new ones. It adds an arcade atmosphere to the game because I'm reminded that on top of the tethers and obsenely large explosions and high octane action, its just an unrealistic and insanely engaging game that asks you to come back and bask in your own shenanigans, if not the records of shenanigans of others.
The map is huge, as one can imagine. I'm not sure that the terrains are improved because I haven't seen the entire map but it blew me away when I saw it.
If you found Just Cause 2 fun, you will find this addictive. If you found Just Cause 2 boring, you will find this slightly appealing because of the wing suit. Don't ♥♥♥♥♥ about it not being realistic, don't kill yourself if its not keeping your attention after five hours (I can't stop playing for some reason), and don't make speeches about how stupid it is.
