In a shorter game the plot would of been fine but here is feels stretched. Asides from that, the game is fun and tense and totally worth it for fans of the survival horror genre or the original film.
Also go watch Alien if you haven't.

Bought an R9 280 and this came with it!
First: WATCH THE MOVIE
- You don't have to but trust me, you will gain a better understanding of the scenario and pick up some references here and there.
Alien: Isolation is an amazing horror experience! Once you first meet the Alien, it's released into the environment and can do whatever the hell it wants. Creeping into the ducts and supprising you when you least expect it. You can even use it to your advantage when faced with hostile survivors, just make a bit of noise and watch the Alien tear up your enemies. It's also good to note that the Alien is COMPLETELY off rails and will be extremely unpredictable.
What doesn't quite work is the constant back tracking required in your objectives. It also seems that the developers put a lot of work into the Alien's AI and slacked off on the survivor's AI. I was faced with a group of three hostile survivors, after stunning one and running off, the other two survivors just stood their staring at their dead friend. They did this for the next twenty minutes without breaking eye contact with the corpse. Not as big of an issue as the game does make up for it with the Alien but it does take out a tiny bit of immersion.
I'd say 8/10 with the missions lacking in flavor. Other than that this is a great game for Alien fans!

After a quick and not-so-enjoyable playthrough of Alien: Colonial Marines, I'm obliged to admit that my hopes for this game where not exactly hightened. However, I was proved quite wrong. Alien: Isolation not only manages to bring this experience to life via the extremely powerful atmosphere that is very present throughout the entire experience, it manages to do so while maintaining enjoyable gameplay, a strong storyline and beautiful ♥♥♥♥ing visuals.
The haunting atmosphere in Alien: Isolation is achieved by a combination of gorgeous graphics, the fear that something is following you constantly, and the amazing use of sound effects. You will be startled by every single ♥♥♥♥ing noise you hear. You will find yourself checking your motion tracker every few seconds, and you will be very grateful for every single bullet you have left. Not that your bullets are of any use against the Alien..
Ultimately, this is what Alien (the film and the games) where supposed to be like. Creating the feeling that you are powerless. Creating the feeling that you are being monitored, and that your life is as fragile as an ant's. This is what Isolation does.
The optimization. Isolation is a fantastic port, it runs at 60 FPS on high settings at 1920x1080p resolution on my machine (GTX 750 Ti 2GB GoldenSample, 6GB DDR2 RAM, AMD Athlon II X3 455 3.3GHz, Windows 7 Utlimate 64 bit)
So yes, it runs amazing which is remarkable, because the game looks stunning..
I'm 8 hours into the game, and I love it. I highly recommended you try this game out. In my opinion, it's damn worth it. I sincerely hope this short review helped someone out

This game is free. Free. And for what it offers, you really won't be disappointed that you picked it up.
The combat system is solid and not complex in the slightest; your basic attack is executed simply by using your directional buttons to walk into an enemy. As the game progresses, you also get provided with extra skills that allow you to do more damage and do area of effect damage, amongst other things. It's really easy to learn, and pretty satisfying once you get the hang of it.
Everyone out there who has played RPGs before will know that grinding is often a huge part of the experience in order to fully enjoy the game. The developer took this into account and created the concept of the arcane areas, which basically allow you to fight through rooms of enemies to acquire materials and experience which are necessary to make the higher tier gear available in the game. That said, the higher tier gear can make most enemies really easy, but the bosses still frequently gave me trouble, even with some of the best items in the game at my disposal.
As for the story, this is where the game really does an amazing job. The characters are developed incredibly well. The quest that Senia, the protagonist, has gone on proceedingly becomes more and more clear, and the implications of her success or failure become equally important to the player as they progress throughout the game. I found myself rooting for her to succeed right to the end. The game also boasts three separate endings depending on your actions towards the end of the game, and each of them are true to the characters, in different ways.
If you're still reading this and haven't downloaded the game yet, let me say it once more. This game is worth your time.

Review is written on Version: 0.3.2.0. Release Date: 19 December 2015.
This is literally the first Early Access game I can consider good and playable and I have seen a fair share of them.
The game is fun, it's meant to have interaction with other players etc so PvP and perhaps even PvE can be done.
The game performs very well even on avarage hardware, 60 FPS is a must and minimum for any game and this game delivers it.
As this is Early Access there is little content available and it took me and my friend less than a day to get all the best gear, items, cars etc in the game and build a nice looking bases as well, but this is completely understandable and expected.
We played on a Community Hosted Server which is a great addition and hopefully as the game gets more popular, more and more of Community Hosted servers get more players in them. As of currently, most of them are basically empty.
The game has very flexible modding support which I personally believe is also a must in any game because that provides potentially evergrowing new content support.
While we played it with my friend, we found suprisingly few bugs, most of them were graphical glitches which do not affect gameplay much at all and the few game bugs we found are very small ones.
The only worries that are present are the ones which you get on any Early Access Game: Hopefully the game development continues at a decent speed (new content gets added, new features etc) and performance of the game won't downgrade over time. So shoutout to Developers: Do NOT back off from this game, finish it, it has great potential!
Would I recommend to play the game in the current state? Yes, it is fun, even with the little content it has to offer right now. This game can potentially be extremely popular especially if the performance factor can be held, both Client and Server side.

A game reminiscent of deck-building games such as Dominion with a little bit of Magic.
The premisce is pretty simple: you have a deck with money and heroes. Using money, you buy more money or heroes and shuffle them back into your deck; when your deck runs out, you reshuffle it and draw from your new deck, hoping to utilize the new cards you've added in to earn victory points. Hero cards are the 'action' cards with special effects, with a good slew of heroes adding attack power which lets you defeat monster cards with their own slew of special effects as well as adding victory points of their own. The goal is to strike the right balance of money and heroes (and constructs) so that you can score victory points as fast as possible.
Though the idea is simple enough, the execution is a bit tougher. There are hundreds of cards across about a dozen 'expansions' and trying to learn them all requires quite the learning curve. You do not have to play with all the expansions at once, and you are able to limit how many are in play at once - some would argue this makes the game better, as expansions have cards that work with each other within expansions, but not always out of expansions. Fortunately, you can zoom in on cards to read their effects as well as being able to use offline practice to warm up.
This is actually a pretty in-depth and strong game, so readers may be wondering why the overall review is so mixed, and it isn't hard to see why. The game is plagued by a few bugs, including one that occurs whenever a card gives you one of two options; the card will instead freeze, and leave you unable to select it until you quit and come back.
The interface is also a bit questionable. A card will sometimes request an action from you, but it will be unclear what that action is (unless you know the card). Card text is very small, making things hard to check without zooming in. There are a lot of functions, including checking through discard piles and opponent's face-up constructs, but you'd never guess the options were there by the way the game is laid out.
Lastly, there is no fullscreen button. This is a detriment, as it would solve the problem of text being too small, and overall make the game easier to focus on.
However, while the game makes faults in terms of its UI and has a few bugs, the game itself is interesting and stands strong. It's not as personal as playing in real life where you can check what cards an opponent has or ask questions (no chat system), but having auto-shuffles and quick play are good advantages of playing an E-card game. In fact, for all the UI's faults, there are virtually no loading times of ANY kind, allowing one to jump from game to game with incredible ease.
Lesser games have gotten paned for sloppy presentation, but the gameplay of Ascension is strong enough that I can recommend this game. However, it is best to play with a friend: card games, even online, are hardly fun alone.

In my opinion this is the best golf game available. I own others but now only play this one. The big difference for me is the swing mechanic. Other games I have played recently (such as TGC) are OK but the swing on those just seems so easy - also like you go on auto-pilot when swinging - and gets a little boring. Not so with Perfect Golf as you need to pay attention to your swing.
I also like that the physics of the game determine where the ball ends up - it is not predetermined as some other games are.
Graphics are decent as well, but I don't have a high end video card and so cannot comment much on that aspect. All I can say is that it is comparable to other recent PC golf titles I have played.
As for the number and variety of courses, it is getting better now with more user-designed courses being released.  In my opinion the variety and quality of courses is what is important rather than sheer numbers. Currently, even in early access, I see variety of courses in Perfect Golf getting better and better. They are quality tracks with a good range of difficulties available.  As the Perfect Golf course designing community grows there will be even more courses of varying visual styles getting released on top of an already great set of courses.

I have been playing Tiger Woods '08 PC on a regular basis since it came out back in 2007.  No modern golf game has come close.  That is until PerfectGolf was released.
The graphics are top notch and very realistic.  You can see all of the undulations and slopes on the fairways/greens very clearly unlike some golf games.  The addition of trees and bushes from SpeedTree last year improved the visuals a great deal.  The graphic improvements will no doubt continue in the future with the possible addition of 3D blades of grass using Nvidia’s Turf Effects tool.
The newly implemented Real Time Swing for controller and mouse has enhanced the game immeasurably in addition to the availability to download fine user made courses (around 24 available as of the date of this review).  That brings the current number of stock and user made courses up to around 37, a number no other modern golf game can touch.  These course numbers will continue to grow and grow once the CourseForge tool comes out and also once the developers start making licensed courses available.
Online play is great with turn based multiplayer and the ability to tee off with up to 8 players.  You can stop and resume your round at a later time.  There are loads of different play modes available in PerfectGolf.  If tournaments are your thing you can participate in many online as well as ones on
.  The game also has a cool replay feature that allows you to watch the last shot from a number of different angles.  Your opponent(s) can see the replays as well.
Another big plus for PerfectGolf is the freecam mode which allows you to more effectively read putts and scope out your next shot, even while your online opponent is getting ready to hit.  Take a virtual tour of the entire course from every conceivable angle and soak in the wonderful immersion that this game provides.
PerfectGolf has lived up to its potential as superb golf simulation.  Every update over the last year has shown improvement, especially the most recent update from last month.  This community driven game will only get better in the months and years to come.  Be sure to give it a try and you won't be disappointed.

Alien: Isolation just ticks over the "Yes" on the recommend question for the detail, atmosphere, and quality.
The reason that it's a borderline "No"? In short, it's the Xenomorph's artificial 'intelligence.' Before I get into the details of that, I want to preface this with, as a gamer, when the option to stealth and/or play non-lethally is available in a game, I take it. Even though it often means nearly doubling the time it takes to complete a game, I enjoy the cautious, cerebral approach to remaining undetected. Some recent examples include Deus Ex (all 3), Dishonored, Thief, and so on.
To that end, I approached my gameplay in Alien: Isolation as purely stealth. But, in the end, my game sessions tend to be far shorter with Alien Isolation than with nearly any other new title I've played in recent memory. The AI used to govern the Xenomorph feels very cheaty.
Unpredictable is one thing: tailing the enemy to a "T" intersection, only to have the enemy turn 180 degrees instead of going left or right down the perpendicular hallway, but that decision changing each time the choice is available; learning your methods of distraction and using that to lure you into it's own trap; jumping up into the ducts, only for it to drop out of the ducts on the other side of the room behind you in a feint/attack menuever.
But too often in Alien Isolation, the Xenomorph AI feels like it cheats and operates on triggers, or pure luck. Here are two examples:
1. While exploring medical facilities, there are two major sections separated by a key card access-only door. Upon finally unlocking the door, I used a distraction device (the first time I even used a gadget against the Xeno) to lure it to the far end of the first part of the facility, and then stealthed to the new section. Upon entering the new section of the facility, without warning, the alien drops right in front of me for an instant death. Now, LOGICALLY speaking, I have provided no evidence to the AI that I'd moved onto a new section of the map (not a level transition), and yet, here is the creature, not only entering the new section, but essentially knowing exactly where I HAVE to enter the facility and entering and killing me before I have a chance to react.
2. A little later I am on a new floor, still in the medical facility, where I need to get my hands on a triage kit. Dealing with both human enemies and the Xeno simultaneously, I utilize a few traps to lure the two into conflict, taking care of the human enemies and leaving only the Xeno to keep track of. After obtaining the kit, I decide to finish exploring this area before moving on, so I carefully listen for the Xeno's movements, and tracking it with the motion tracker when it's far enough away to not hear it. I come into a large room, moving from one hiding spot to the other, all the while tracking the Xeno. I'm in a spot just a few feet from a terminal, watch the motion tracker for a moment to watch the Xeno, scrambling through the vents, speed out of range. I interact with the computer, and as has become my MO, quickly scroll through all the available entries to read later in a safe hiding spot. I don't get past the second entry (no more than 6 seconds since watching the Xeno run out of range on the motion tracker), and I hear it drop out of a vent directly behind me, then eviscerating me only a few heartbeats after I've managed to back out of the terminal.
These are just two highly illustrative exampes of several that leave me highly frustrated after only a 1-3 hour gaming session. Either one or both of the following is true: it doesn't matter how stealthy and sneaky you are, the AI knows what your next objective is and is programmed to get in your way, with only minimal regard to what you've done to try and cause distractions/impediments. Or, when you are being ultra stealthy and would otherwise have no other reason to be detected, a random number generator is being used to determine whether or not the alien is going to 'randomly' ambush you, leaving you stuck with a total reliance on pure chance on whether or not your next step is going to be your last.
I haven't finished the game yet, nor have I gotten the (what should be entirely optional) flamethrower to fend off an alien attack; but I do intend to finish. I just think its going to take me a lot longer than usual due to the frustrating nature of the AI.
An unpredictable but logical AI can provide a great challenge and a certain dynamism to gameplay. But unpredictability coupled with illogical cause/effect (or lack of cause for effect) is just downright aggravating.
Ultimately, I lean just barely on the side of recommend with a hefty asterisk warning you about the aggravating nature of the widely-tauted Xenomorph AI.

TL;DR: In general - if you liked the first Dishonored and don't mind (or in fact want) more of the same - Dishonored 2 is for you. If you are looking for innovations, new gameplay, etc - sadly, you won't find much of it here
Dishonored 2 is a second installment of one of my favorite games of 2012.
It's a stealth action FPS game, that can scratch that Thief itch, and spice it with a mix of Deus-Ex like mechanics and approaches to level design.
Pros:
- Gameplay is great (especially so if you enjoyed the first part, absolutely nails stealth mechanics)
- There are some new powers to play with (e.g. Corvo can possess corpses, Emily has full set of new powers that are nonetheless quite similar to Corvo's - e.g. Corvo stops time, Emily stops enemies)
- Amazing level design (especially shape-shifting Clockwork mansion and time-travel in Stilton's manor)
- Variety of approaches and playstyles that can scratch just about any FPS itch, as well as provide loads of replay value
Neutral:
- It's kind of more of the same (nothing stands out quite as much as the first game)
- Storyline is pretty much same (for Corvo almost identical - you have to save Emily again) and doesn't change with selected character much
- Chaos system doesn't seem to affect that much (in contrast with Dishonored 1)
- Graphics was not massively upgraded (yet performance was that poor at the start)
- No "New Game+", but it was promised in upcoming update in December 2016
Cons:
- Performance was abysmal, got better after the patch, still kinda shaky

Short but pleasant action game.
Both the story and characters are great. Sad and tragic, yet portrays valiant heroism. Every major character (excluding bosses) are interesting and well drawn. The only exception to this is the tutorial fairy, but I've checkmarked it as comedic relief.
But most importantly, the gameplay is solid. Controls feel fluid, and the learning curve is very low for a fast paced ARPG. However, I'm not too fond of 'progress to next world, craft equipment that's strictly better' since this sort of progression actually makes overleveling a problem; it turns the "regular game" where you grind monsters into a literal grind instead of an interesting battle using both normal attacks and skills. Luckily, this is redeemed with 'hard mode' boss fights where it's impossible to become overlevelled at. Thus, my only complaint about the difficulty is that there's no 'hard mode everything' to balance the game's leveling system. Otherwise, boss fights are extremely exciting and creates an intense atmosphere.
Overall, great game. For originating in Asia, the english translation is nicely done. If you haven't played this game already, it's free! There's no reason not to unless you absolutely can't stand a bit of RPG grinding.

I am stupid. I am a very stupid person. You can say it. I want you to say it.

With the advent of the Real Time Swing control interfaces, Perfect Golf has established itself as a major player in the golf game market.  It was already a solid performer with its 3-click and Motion Swing (mouse) swing interfaces. but the all new Real Time Swing - Mouse (RTS-Ml) and Real Time Swing - Controller (RTS-C) broadens the appeal of the game by more dynamically engaging the senses in a live process.
Both RTS-C and RTS-M require a sensual mastery over an analog control mechanism that has a reasonable and rewarding learning curve.  There are also 5 levels of difficulty to help you wade into the world of real time swing interfaces at a level suited to any skill set.  I've been a real time swing controller fan since Links 2004 on the original XBox, and Perfect Golf's RTS-C has finally taken a controller swing interface through the portal that Links 2004's opened and added dimensions to its performance that uncannily model the nuances of a golf swing in a manner I wouldn't have ever dreamed would be possible with a controller.
I'm a slightly better than average skill player, and I've managed to break par only 3 times in 50+ rounds, using "Hacker" difficulty (the scale runs Beginner, Hacker, Amateur, Pro, Tour Pro) with my XBox 360 wired controller.  Some would say that someone who's used to shooting 62 - 66 in a computer golf game would be frustrated by this.  Au contraire, I find it stimulating to be challenged to fully think out and execute every shot.  A fairway or green in regulation is something you don't take for granted with RTS-C.  What keeps me going is I am seeing a gradual improvement in my game as I become more familiar with the intricately scaled analog interace the game uses.  I'm probably only a few weeks away from stepping up to Amateur!
Perfect Golf has so much more to offer besides its cutting edge interface options.  Its course creation suite called "Course Forge" has already given birth to a couple dozen user created courses, many of which are commercial quality.  RobC's Bandon Dunes is as good as any of the stock courses that come with the game.  PG also has a bevy of multiplayer options in its Multiplayer Lobby, in addition to having an ongoing chat room from which you can discuss the game and learn from others.  There's also a facility to support user created tournaments that is proving to be popular with community sites like
, which hosts a number of Tours and Tournaments of various difficulty and control types, in addition to reviewing and hosting downloadable, user created courses.
Keep in mind that Perfect Golf is still in Early Access and is still being refined.  It's highly playable in its current form, but it's also interesting to see the degree of enhancements this game is getting in these final stages.  The developers are also open to user input in these final stages of the game's birth so feel free to sign up at
and weigh in with your opinions, experiences, and suggestions.   Whether you're a casual player or a die-hard sim-head, You're not going to find a better value for $19.99!

The key to deciding whether you should buy this game is whether you like golf.  Real life golf is frustrating, but very rewarding if you can achieve success, and to do that, it takes some work.  This game is the same way, you have to put some time in to get some success - but it can be fun on the way due to the high quality courses available upon which to play.  I have been pleasantly surprised by the quailty of the courses, both the ones supplied by default in the game, and the user designed courses which so far have proven to be of as high a quality as the default courses.
My favorite method of play (swing type) is the newly implemented Real Time Swing - Motion Swing which is proving to be very immersive giving you the feeling that you are really on a golf course and not sitting in front of a computer.
Some of the new courses and swing type changes is stirring more interest in this game and there is quite a community of active players who hang out in the lobby for online multiplayer games.  There is also a site which offers weekly tournaments seemlessly integrated into the game with nearly 100 players signed up at the tour pro level (the one I play).  I do not know how many play in the other level tournaments, I suspect that it is 100s more.  There are currently no additional costs to fully participate in the game, courses, lobby or tournaments (although the tournament host does solicit donations on the website through a button).  Eventually there will be premium content for purchase (licensed courses, and accesories which will only be cosmetic and not give you an advantage in the game), but that content will not be necessary to enjoy the game.
There will be a program called course forge which will allow anyone who purchases this game to design beautiful course the same way that the original ones were developed.  The current crop of user developed courses were designed by beta testers of course forge.  Course forge will come out when the game exits Early Access, probably sometime this year (but don't quote me).
Pluses - gameplay is rich, not repetitive, due to realistic physics and variability
interest in the game is growing, lots of partners/opponents available
developer is active, listens to gamers suggestions and incorporates improvements
game works on multiple platforms including golf simulators
Minuses - game requires modern computer graphics power to enjoy smooth gameplay
players who want instant gratification may be disappointed with learning curve
My advice is to purchase this game while it is still in Early Access as it will surely be more than $20 when it is fully released.

Surprisingly addictive, what a fantastic resource gathering/building system!
Seriously, developers of other games should see how mining/building/research is done here and take a lesson.
Also the performance on it is amazing, early access or no, load times were incredibly fast and there were no lag issues at all.  I did experience a wierd 'fall through the world' thing, but to be fair, I think I'd left the game on for some 20 hours and after relogging, this didn't happen again.
We had a load of fun unlocking all the upgrades/vehicles, puzzling through the 'chemistry' system of what gas/liquid/etc. makes what, seeking out and finding rare resources, setting up trade routes to our main base, and of course building/designing the main base.
I imagine that for those who like the whole pvp thing, there's many more hours of fun here.  Playing it as a single player/duo non-conflict building game will net you a reasonable amount of enjoyment but there's no real replay value after that, sadly.
I was dubious at first about the fact that you control a vehicle rather than a character, and felt a lack of character identity throughout my play, just hopping from vehicle to vehicle.   There's no sort of experience/skill/advancement here, just faction based research to unlock more equipment.   Unless you're in it for the competitive aspect, you will run out of things to do, despite this I certainly feel like I got my money's worth.   After a week of binge-play though, having unlocked everything and such, I find there's nothing really to do, as there's no real pve-type content, no character development, and our base was 'done'.  I completely understand that what I wanted out of this game is not necessarily what is intended though, so can't fault it for me 'playing it wrong'. :X    I reached this same point with Conan Exiles, Dark and Light, Citadel Forged with Fire, etc. etc.  If you're into the whole survival/pvp thing though this seems like a great starting point for that sort of play.

I really enjoy this game and its adventureing and base building aspects. It's also a game you can play to your own style as well. Go as slow as you want or as fast as you can, to get the biggest and best tech and vehicles. You can also customize your vehicle colors and some of its equipment as well! Honestly though its really all about the vehicles which there are a good number and variety of with more to come.
Personally i am really looking forward to where this game is going and the kind of content that will be added (moar boats please!). The game seems suprisingly involved in chemestry (its made easy, you dont need to actually know any science so dont get scared) which i find really cool. You also have to figure out how to make certain elements to make other elements which is also really cool. No ammonia? Make it!
While singleplayer is rather lonely and empty, albeit with some aliens to give some reason to have weapons, online has actually turned out to be rather enjoyable, if a bit crowded after awhile. With that said you can open up your singlepalyer game to your friends to releave some of that lonelyness.
Previously i had an issue with bandit type players making my experience misserable, but it seems i was just unlucky and got the attention of some bad apple starting out. As such the biggest issue i had, the other players, is no not such a large issue. Also at the end of it they are really more annoyances than issues. As such me giving the game more time i have come accorss an suprisly good number of nice players who are quite helpful and not out to get off from wrecking other peoples stuff for no reason. They actually want a reason to fight someone or have a mutual agreement to do it. You know like normal people.
They do have a system in place where your base(s) cannot be captured for 48 hours after you or someone in your faction visits them. This timer resets every time you visit a base, which i find kinda awesome. However theres little to stop them simply coming in and wrecking and robbing you until about mid game where you get base defense and containers that cant be robbed. Thjis is a game mechanic i have come to accept and while it can be abused towards the lower tech palyers i think its not as much of an issue as it seems.
At first i said 'dont play online unless you have a group of people to play with' basically. now though i see that its really nice to be able to play online with tohers as while my first impression was probably the worst one i could get of them, i have seen that i only encountered a small minority of people in this game who are like that. However i think is something that can never fully be 'solved' you are always going to have bad people who have every right to play the game how they want as you do. Now the bigget let down is when they rest the servers after it gets too crowded but is a neccesary thing as the game progresses.
So some of the pros and cons for me in this game and some thing i would like to see improved or added to the game are;
Pros
- Base building and management
- Suprisingly massive world
- Go at your own pace
- Georgeous scenery and vehicles
- Technolgies give you direction and meaning for going out and exploring to find new minerals
- Creative mode to let you play around as much as you'd like
- Decent music
- Dynamic weather
- Well Optimized
- Randomly spawned trading depots you have to find and which gives money a useful purpose.
- World that reacts to your pollution. Cause too much, aliens get♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥and some of your techs wont work as well in it.
- You can make trade routes with your other bases and other friendly palyer bases so you can automatically transport materials between them or trade for materials with other players.
Cons
- Rather empty and somewhat boring world.
- Only 2 types of boats/ships at the time of this review.
- Somewhat repetative
- Large open world also means long travel times. Gets better once you get aircraft. Honestly this isn't that much of a con, more of a 'neccessary inconvenience'.
- Weapons arn't practical or useful until you get to mid game.
- Game is really all about base building and collecting vehicles at this time which isn't a bad thing.
- Lack of explanations/tutorials or hints leave you to figure out the game on your own or ask other how the game works.
- No load or save buttons, while it does save your worlds you have to remember what you named them and retype that everytime you open the game for singleplayer.
- Draw/render distance is shorter than i would like it to be.
- Currently no modding support.
- Trying to place structures or foundations when building base is a bit glitchy and frustrating sometimes.
Improvements/additions i would like to see;
- A wench to help get unstuck and tow other players.
- Farther render/draw distance.
- More vehicles and variety of vehicles, Fixed wing planes, tracked vehicles, moar boats.
- 1st person view or shoulder view.
- Anti-grief system or incentive not to be one. Reward people for being good people!
- Buildings/structures/tech that would encourage more interaction between players in non agressive ways. Like a building that would send AI vehicles out to do trade missions to trade connected bases.
- Profanity Filter.
- Modding support.
- Animals/Wildlife.
- Tutorial or help menu to learn the game mechanics
- More entities to interact with in the world, like AI factions.
- Interior lighting

I've been a longtime fan of the Just Cause series, and really loved Just Cause 2. However Just Cause 3 is interesting as it almost doesn't feel like a sequal to JC2, but instead to the original Just Cause. JC3 has sort of gone back to its roots in a lot of ways. However this presents both good and bad things:
Pros:
-Explosions are great and bigger than ever
-Many new ways to create explosions and kill enemies
-New Grapple is amazing, allows you to connect multiple objects at once and use that to your advantage
-The Addition of the Wingsuit is new and very fun to fly around with
-The Rebel Drop system is fast and effiecient, and if you want more rebel drops or to get certain drops faster you can get gears to achieve this (In comparison to JC2, which required money to get drops, and usually a lot of it)
-Lots of new great vehicles and weapons that create even better explosions
Cons:
-Graphics didn't seem like much of a step up from JC2.
-Pretty bad optimization on release (Some of these issues are still present), even on Low I had some FPS problems. Looking at specs my rig shoulda been able to run this at least on Medium at 50-60 FPS.
-The map was not any bigger than JC2, this wouldn't have been an issue for me, however inside JC2's map was much more content, with more settlements, towns, and cities it seemed a lot more populated within the 1000 KM. Area. JC3, with the same Area, had a lot less cities and settlements within the open world, however it did have a good amount of military bases in both games.
So, Overall I think the game is very fun, but defin. has its issues. I am happy I bought the game, but not sure if everybody would enjoy it. (However you may or may not have the same optimization issues as I did). I'd give the game a 6.5/10.

Alien Isolation has exceeded my expectations which I find extremeley rare in the gaming industry today.  There are not many games that have held me and surprised me as much as this one. Real authenticity, atmosphere, terror and pure adreneline pumping action that will have you on the edge of your seat for hours.  The survival genre has had it's bar set to a new high.  As a massive fan of the films I am honored to have such a title apart of the Alien franchise.  The game oozes the true authentic style of the 1979 film and has a gripping soundtrack.  Graphics are solid and the lighting in the game is some of the best work I have seen.  The story and lore is well placed and I don't remember anything not making perfect sense.  Having just finished the game I would say it's easily one of my games of 2014.  My playing experience included very few bugs and anomolies.  This I am very happy with.  A big thank you to Creative Assembly, you nailed it!

Despite the annotations that come with recommending this game, I will honestly say that I recommend giving All Points Bulletin: Reloaded a try.
The story of APB: Reloaded is a long and painful one, but essentially this game was the fever dream of a game developer who made a very famous game (and by proxy a very famous series) into a reality - and it was perfect... on paper. In execution All Points Bulletin was very sloppy. While the game's concept was amazing, Grand Theft Auto meets Crackdown in an open world MMO environment, essentially a massively multiplayer online cops vs. robbers. The game was originally developed by Realtime Worlds, and this game is, from what I know, solely responsible for that company's destruction.
It was a multi million dollar budget going into a fever dream, and the execution was not great.
When Realtime Worlds fell apart and the All Points Bulletin servers were being shut down as a result, a company named Reloaded Productions bought the rights in a panic. Perhaps they were hoping to unlock this game's great potential, and to some extent they managed. However, it's still not perfect.
In APB: Reloaded you get to create and fully customize (through means of in-game progression based on PVP wins and actions you do around the city) a character of your own design, essentially meaning you can fully express yourself to any extent you want. Clothes, hair styles, hair colours, makeup, the colour on your clothes, cars, emblems of your own design that you can put on your clothes and your vehicles, and much more - all so that you can express your own personality while kicking tail against other players in a rather populated world. There are two factions to choose from, as this is a cops vs. robbers game -- Criminals, who get to run around mugging AI civilians, breaking into stores, and stealing cars for money as well as the actions they commit in the PVP missions, and Enforcers, who get to run around stopping Criminals from commiting crimes and by proxy earning money. In APB: Reloaded, your actions affect other players, and your progression is directly a result of other players. I find this a very fun and very interesting concept. However, guns don't have a realistic amount of kick or damage values against other players and you might often hear the argument that they feel more like airsoft guns than real ones. The leaning system in combat with other players is pulled off really well, to the extent that it can be really frustrating to fight other players as they just crouch down and lean to one side, making it extremely difficult to hit them in the fast-paced mid-range firefights you'll get into. To make that matter worse, they can change shoulders. Of course, I'm not complaining - this is, in my opinion, a wonderful system and it adds so much more diversity and change to a combat system that would otherwise be too repetitive and boring for anyone to care. APB, on top of this, offers live events for rewards - something like a package somewhere in the city to pick up, and you have to pick it up and bring it to your person while everyone else tries to kill you for it. However, keep in mind - when Reloaded acquired the rights for All Points Bulletin and took over development, APB: Reloaded became free to play. With a free to play game this big, unsurprisingly, the developers have to make money somehow. This factors in the pay to win aspect that is honestly, in my eyes, not too overpowered or overdone. Essentially, you pay a little real money and you get more in-game money, more in-game experience, and you can even buy progress with the NPCs you're trying to get rep from, pushing your progression along a lot more quickly than other players. This doesn't mean it's impossible for a completely free-to-play player to lock you down in every aspect right off the bat, however, because the best guns in APB do not necessarily mean the highest chances of winning. And in terms of progression, this game is very grindy. That's not something I particularly take issue with, but it's something to keep in mind if you plan on trying this game out -- which of course I believe you should. The thing with a game as grindy as this is, if you focus on the grind it's going to be very difficult and very frustrating for you. Things take a long time to go through, especially with the matchmaking and ranking system being based on in-a-row wins and losses, which is highly abused by high-skill players who want an easy game, as all they have to do is lose a few times intentionally and wind up facing newbies who have little to no chance of beating them. However, with all the tropes I have with this game, it's a very fun and very addicting title. Don't pay attention to the grind - pay attention to the action/reaction of the in-game world around you and use other players to grind without focusing too much on the fact that, at its core, that is what you're doing.
Overall, I would give this game a 7/10 and definitely recommend it - despite what you'll hear from a lot of other players and companies, this game is a very good and very unique experience. I personally love it, and it's worth a try if you've never played it before.

that most people probably wouldn't care about, but let me give you the short and sweet! That said, I'm not going to go into the story of the game all that much, as I could probably go on and on about the world and stories within the game.
Dishonored 2 is a sequel to one of my all-time favourite games, and it manages improve on almost every point of the original game.
Dishonored 2 is set in the city of Karnaca, on the island of Serkonos. It's a very different place than Dunwall of Dishonored 1, but it's a very interesting location. Calling Karnaca an improvement over Dunwall is probably not the proper way to talk about it, as it's very different. It's lighter and more colourful, but it's still a Dishonored game, which means there's some pretty grim and dark things going on, and you see that instantly when you get to Karnaca.
the sequal improves on more or less everything; giving the player more options to play the way you want. Stealth has been improved quite a bit, and there's new upgrades to both your physical and supernatural powers. It still playes alot like the first game, but it feels expanded upon in every way.
But maybe the biggest change from the first game is the option to pick between playing as Corvo or the new character of Emily Kaldwin. Both having different set of supernatural powers to play around with, giving you two slightly different playstyles and experiences.
Dishonored 2 isn't a bad looking game, even on the lower settings the game looks pretty damn good in my opinion. This could be thanks to the game's somewhat unusual mix of realistic and caricature artstyle, this similar to how it was in Dishonored 1, but very much improved alot. Some of these graphical improvements are thanks to the change to their new game engine named "Void Engine", which is a heavily modified version of the iD Tech 5 engine.
this has probably been the roughest spot for the game. On launch it was plagued by alot of inconsistent performance issues across alot of PC setups, it didn't matter if you had a low-medium end machine or the newest of new components, the game ran poorly. Thankfully (at the time of writing) this has been or is currently being fixed, thanks to the current Beta Patch. It's still not running perfectly, but overall running WAY better than it used to during the launch week.
as stated in the opening, I'm not going to go super deep into the story, as I've only played Emily's side of it so far, and still haven't gotten to the end of it yet. I will probably go back and edit this section when I finish the game.
That said, I'm really enjoying it. It's a bit different from the revenge story of the first game, this thanks to the introductions of voiced protagonists which gives the characters a bit more life and personalities.
It might be the story of Dishonored 2 that is the weakest point for me, but that was the same for me with the first game.
It's not fantastic, but it's pretty good. One of the issues of the story is that it feels like some of the mission is cut just a tad short, resulting in some of the characters you run into lack just a little bit of character development.
The main story itself is kind of predictable, not throwing all that many curveballs in your direction and ends up falling just a bit short yet again. There might be some big twist at the end of the game, but as of writing I'm probably a couple of hours away from the ending.
Dishonored 2 is a fantastic game, it's a welcome and great sequel to one of my all-time favourite new titles. The World of Dishonored 2 is interesting, filled with weirdness, occult mysteries and stealthy action. It's sadly had a rough start with massive performence issues, but these issues have been fixed to some extent.
Do I recommend Dishonored 2? If you love games that give you multiple options to solve a problem; love stealth-action; interesting immersive world. This is a game for you.

UPDATED: Dark Souls II is fairly enteraining, yet surprisingly easy. If you've never played a Souls game before, I strongly suggest starting with this one. This Souls game was much easier to grasp then its predecessors, Dark Souls and Demon's Souls. It's combat mechanics are much more fluent, which makes up for it's lack of creative enemies. Every area has a new mob enemy to try and kill and gain knowledge on, but they also seem a lot less punishing, unless your facing 7 or 10 of them. From invisble warriors to possessed spider people. After playing a couple of dozen hours now, and having read much of the other reviews here, i just can say
buy the game it´s totally worth it´s money with patch 12 being out.
Many of the negative reviews here are just silly hateboy drivvel, some of them are just plain wrong and outright ridiculous.
So get things straight:
1. Compared to Shogun 2, its a lot more stable; i kept having the famous autosave crash during the whole shogun 2 series , even with fall of the samurai every second autosave. Just once( !!!!) in rome 2, using the cloud for save.
2. Some people complained that the game engine obviously comes from Empire, and wasnt therefore suited to melee warfare. Well, pure hogwash, Shogun 2 had the same Empire engine, and melee worked just fine!
3. The premade tactical formations in battles work extremely good, and are very realistic. Frankly 80 % of all real battles in antiquity worked like phalanx in the front and cavalry on the flanks, skirmisher screen in front. If the main line budged, or the flanks got lost, battle was lost. The game here pretty much works the same way, it´s astonishing how well the engine emulates that logic of ancient phalanx/maniple warfare.
4. The new region system saves you a lot of micromanagement and is frankly more realistic. On the downside, you cant fortify every border town anymore, but that just makes proper strategic planning and gaining client states or satrapies more important, since you cant defend each settlement.
Well, the naval battles are quite crappy, but heh, no cannon broadsides without cannons, and ancient sea battles resembled a crazed ramming and boarding contest anyway. And rest assured, as soon as you got ships with on deck artillery, the transport rush thing is over. Besides, the often mentioned super transports can barely survive 3 rammings, whereas a quinquireme or somesuch can easily take a dozen hits. And transports tend to burn down real quick, therefore you just do need a real navy after the opening phase of the campaign.
So yeah, the game is totally worth it´s money now, and i´d dare say it´s one of the best in the series in her current patched state( 12 patches lol, was the original qualitiy assurance done by drunken monkeys?) with more content coming up every 2 months or so.
Haven´t played the Gaul and Hannibal campaign yet, gonna buy them with the next steam sale, and will write  probably a review about that too.
p.s. patch 14(!!!!) out , a real big one commited just on artificial dumbness for siege battles. The comp attacking your walled cities was one of the weak points of this game; I kept butchering 4k plus barbarian armies with just a few units behind the walls repeatedly for example. So a real good game probably just got a lot better.

There are many things I love about this game & there's been a few really great additions to the core concepts that I hope will be carried on into future TW titles.
That said, the only thing missing here is the Family Tree system. It's a major drawback in my opinion. Without it, you feel completely detatched from your generals. They are just sprites - nothing more. No longer can you found a dynasty that will last hundreds of years, diplomatically marrying off your children for political gain or avenging your father King who fell in battle with enemy.
If you're completely new to Total War then I recommend buying this game, it's not terrible, especially now given that there's a million great mods out there for you to try that offer all kinds of improvements. But if you're already a fan of the previous installments and you're not too sure about Rome II then you might want to consider skipping this one. Stick to Rome I, Medieval II or Shogun II.
From what I've gathered, CA have attempted to streamline the game to fit a wider audience rather than listen to the die-hard TW fans.
Let's hope they take from this experience and make the next TW game the masterpiece that it should be!

Nope. Tried to at least get some enjoyment out of this but all the bosses I played are awful and the levels don't tend to be much better.
The controls are really stiff and the game expects rather precise platforming out of you on a few occasions, random difficulty spikes in an otherwise kind of tame platforming game. A fair few of the levels are pretty tedious, to boot; one level I played had me going back three times through the same area to move cubes around, with basically no danger, followed up by a relatively dangerous two sections afterwards. That doesn't make a game harder, it just makes it more boring.
The bosses, though. The first one is... okay, if not a little broken. The second is basically chance, you have to jump early and pray that you get the exact angle you need, and the boss is completely random so he can dodge out of the way of a successful attack sometimes, or spend a lot of time using attacks where you can't fight back. The third, though... a loooong autoscroll that only has real danger about a minute in, and then a moment that was as far as I got where you have to press a button and then go BACKWARDS to grab a cube. At that level of failing to understand basic game design, I just up and quit. Not worth my time, nor my money.
The aesthetic is decent, though not that special, and the soundtrack is okay as well. But I was just not getting any enjoyment out of this, even for the low price tag.
EDIT: I'm persistent as heck so I went and finished the game. It doesn't get better. There's a pure trial-and-error level that you literally have to replay until you've memorized, a ton of really picky platforming bits combined with the game's awful auto-jump and touchy engine, the final boss has a huge RNG element to it, a lot of levels go on too long for their own good, a few levels have puzzles where failure means restarting after you've already gone through a platforming segment to get to the puzzles, there's overly powerful rocket launchers eventually introduced, some wonky physics stuff with the booster panels, the falling blocks are used horribly in some places, placed at the end of levels with tricky jumps where failure means a full restart... the list just goes on and on, in only 50 levels + 5 bosses there are so many poor game design choices that I just couldn't wring any enjoyment out of this whatsoever.

I went into this game thinking it was a puzzle game with platform elements.
It turns out it is almost entirely a platformer, with maybe two or three puzzles ("Solve 50 unique puzzles on your way"? yeah right). Oh, and one of those puzzles uses mechanics that you aren't introduced to at all. There is no explanation of it, which leads to you having to figure out the complicated mess out on your own. Usually that's not a big deal (especially since I enjoy actual puzzles), but trial and error was made difficult by needing to pass part of the level before you can even attempt the puzzle.
The boss battles aren't very difficult, and are nice additions. Except for the lass boss, which is one of the most frustrating bosses I've ever faced. The boss is actually very easy, all you need to do is dodge some stuff. But he randomly uses a pulse, which is 99% guaranteed to push you into debris; there is also no way to tell when he's about to do it, so it's unavoidable. In other words, you just have to hope that he doesn't use it.
*End rant*
The first 40 levels or so of the game aren't bad. In fact, I enjoyed it. Sure, it was all platforming when I expected puzzles, but that wasn't a huge deal. It was fun.
The last 10 levels and the final boss ruin this game. There are ridiculous timing-based events and several parts that require luck, making the overall experience more frustrating than it's worth.

Highly recommended.  A recent update added quite a few community made courses (along with updates to the stock courses in the game) and also added several new swing styles.
A wide range of swing styles are available:
Traditional 3-click with a power meter
Motion Swing with the mouse that has a meter on the screen (your choice of swinging horizontally or vertically)
Real Time Swing with the mouse (your choice of swinging horizontally or vertically.  No meter on the screen but the player animation moves in concert with the mouse movement)
Real Time Swing with a controller
The game can also be played on a home golf simulator.
The motion swings are my personal favorites.  Tempo has a large part in determining the outcome of the shot (as well as swing path and heel/toe hits)  so it's not as simple as straight back/straight through.  A truly wonderful way to play PC golf.
There are also a wide range of difficulty options so you can jump right in and enjoy the game.  The easier levels are a great introduction to the game.  Casual player or just want to have a fun round?  It's here.

The highest levels of difficulty are quite tough but it doesn't feel unfair or gimmicky.  If you can control your swing, you can still score well.  If you're not playing well, it can be a real grind, but  it is so rewarding when you put a good swing on the ball.  A great option for the hardcore sim player.
The course designs are beautiful and the ball physics are the best I've seen in a PC golf game.  A wide range of stimp settings are available for the green speeds, several firmness settings for the fairways, and several settings for pin positions.
Currently there are about 33 courses in the game, as well as a large driving range and a short game practice area.

The game is still in Early Access so things are still being worked on.  Things not yet included in the game but are planned for the future:
-Career mode
-Assortments of clothing/animations/clubheads/balls/shafts etc...
-Course building software
-More courses
-Improved AI for the CPU players
-Country clubs and tournaments
There currently is a REALLY good third party tournament site that hosts weekly tournaments for various skill levels as well as fun ancillary events.
They have an automatic scoring system set up that will keep track of your scores and stats after each round and maintains them on their site.  They also maintain different tours, world rankings, money leaders, ongoing season stats, etc.. and it's free to join.  A very well run tour.
I'm sure I'm forgetting some things but again, this is a great game.

I never really write reviews but I definitely felt compelled to write one after being immediately dissatisfied with my purchase.
Let me start off by mentioning that I am a HUGE Ascension fan. I have been playing the board game (physical copy) for about 4 years and I am pretty obsessed with it. I own every physical standalone and expansion and and I also have them all on android as well.
I usually ALWAYS read reviews for PC games but seeing what the makers of Ascension have done with the physical games and playdek with the mobile platform I did not hesitate...the moment I heard that it came out I went to steam and purchased it no questions asked. That being said, what Playdek has released for PC is complete garbage. There is literally no other way to describe it.
What I expected: Full screen resolution, crisp graphics, high resolution card art, smooth animation transitions. I was so excited to fire up the game and play it on my 27" monitor with my friends...
What I got: Garbage. The game was obviously ported from mobile app to PC which is like porting an original NES game to  PS4 retaining its 16bit gfx. Its literally a square box that takes up 1/8th of my screen, if you toggle "full screen" you just laugh because it "stretches" the resolution into a bigger square and makes it look like the game was designed in Microsoft Paint. You can barely read the cards...and the animation of the cards moving around, going into play, discarding etc. is horrendous. Its sooooo choppy and laggy it is obnoxious. Explain to me how a game runs this choppy on an Intel i7 with 16gb of ram, and a top notch Nvidia card...Oh...and its installed on an SSD...YOU CANT EXPLAIN IT...it just points purely to HORRIBLE design.
Let's talk about the kickstarter for a moment. My best friend pledged a stupid amount of money for Ascension Online...to the point of him *someday* receiving the entire physical edition in a carved wooden box and every card a foil edition. Well since then they tried to cheapen up the carved wooden box and oh...its been like 2+ years and he still has nothing...then THIS IS WHAT THEY RELEASE?? They made it sound like Playdek was out and they were working with a newer company to release this amazing online version of the platform that was going to blow everyone away...NOT A MOBILE TO PC PORT!
How can they make a game like Solforge and then put this crap out. Playdek if you are going to continue to make crap like this then just say so. Take a look at HEX, take a look at Hearthstone...this is what people EXPECT out of an online card game and honestly in the Kickstarter Stoneblade made it sound like it was going to be comparable to the aformentioned games.
This is a joke. This is not a PC game, this is an insult. DO NOT BUY THIS GAME until IF and WHEN they actually put out a respectable product.

If you are a fan of deckbuilding games, then Ascension may very well be a good game to recommend for you.  It is based off the popular (real) card game and translates well into the digital world.  The object of the game is basically to acquire powerful cards to help you gather points(called honor in this game) and get rid of your weak starting cards at the same time.
I can at the present time recommend this game for anyone interested in these types of games as the developer has slowely delivered extra free content and fixed bugs and other issues.  I wish there was more support and contact between the developer and fanbase but it can't all be perfect.
Pros:
- Based on a great board game and some matches can be fun to play
- Decent multiplayer system that allowslets you play a game against other people at your leisure (you can set timer for quick games that last minutes or others that last days) and it also allows you to play multiple games at once.
- Developer has delivered expansions for the game 6 months after release as well as fixed some very game breaking bugs.
Cons:
- AI is not very good at all.  AI can be very one dimensional at times and is not very good at building a good deck
- No options to set resolutions and other things.  The options menu is very basic
- No volume options.  You either have music or sounds effects off or on.  I like to play with Sound Effects on but since there is no volume slider I can't play music over the game.
- I mentioned the multiplayer system is very nice, but the layout is very clunky.  Wish it was easier to switch between games and play other games.  Maybe some sort of sound bit, or notification on bottom of screen when opponent in other only game has taken a turn.  Currently that is all guesswork.
- Lack of updates.  Although I praised their ability to roll out free new content and fix the worst of the bugs there are still many other bugs that have not been addressed.  A few of the achievements have been broken since Day 1.
- LAG during AI turns.  Sometimes when the AI has its turn it slows down for no discernable reason and it can take the AI very long to complete its turn.  This problem has been ongoing since release and there has been nothing done to address the issue.
EDITED Feb 25th 2015: The game has now been out for 2+ months and there has been very little communication with the developers about the future of this game.  There are posts asking on the forum whether the title has been abandoned.  There was an update released in January about 1 month after release that fixed a few issues, but also created just as many new ones.  The developers are only now asking for feedback after 1 month of this update to fix issues.  I do believe all these issues will eventually be ironed out but it will probably take another 4-6 months.
EDITED Jun 25th 2015:  The game has now been out for 6+ months.  There have been a few updates to the game since my last update as well as the addition of a free new expansion.  I've changed my review from negative to positive even though there are still issues that have not been addressed since release.

Ascension is a great game.  It's a fun strategic drafting/deck-building game that rewards well-thought out strategies which change from game to game.
This game is terrible.  It is a buggy hot mess.  Other reviews have stated that this is a warmed over version of the buggy app and that would explain a lot... but not why Playdek has decided to drop this pile on us just in time for the holidays!
Here's some constructive criticism:
Resolution.  The game won't expand to fit my screen and I find myself straining to see different cards.  Come on guys.  This is just terrible.  What PC game doesn't have a full screen mode?  And one where I might be able to actually read the cards without having to zoom them.  This convinces me that I spent $10 on a half-finished mobile phone app instead of an actual game.
Controls.  Counter-intuitive and and mostly terrible.   I find myself clicking on and buying cards I really didn't want to buy and banishing stuff I would have liked to keep.
Lots of random bugs.  First time I've had to pay for an open alpha test of a game.  Any chance playdek actually tried fixing these before dropping this directly onto our faces?  For their sakes, I hope they didn't because its just terrible.
Online games.  Wow.  Ok... where to begin.  You can't talk to people, it's hard to get games together and everyone seems intent on watching cat videos instead of playing the game.  How hard is it to make a customizable timer?  10 minutes is too few, 30 minutes is perhaps too long for people afking... 15-20 minute timers sound ideal, unless you're Playdek.  I guess the care-o-meter just ran too low at the end of development time and we get stuck alpha testing a mobile app on our PCs.
It's a deeply frustrating experience, which is sad because the underlying game is really fun and has so much potential.
TLDR: Avoid this unless you really like squinting at your computer and testing for glitches.

After returning to the game after a long hiatus, which was based on it not being worth paying a subsciption for, I have decided to write a review. I have not read any of the other reviews here so there may or may not be overlap, but I wanted to say how I feel about it.
-The game in its current form has exceptionally good graphics, easily the best in any MMO I have played.
- The generic user interface is simple to the point of not displaying pertinent information until the game thinks you need    it. ie, your experience bar...
-Targeting in combat is clunky and sometimes difficult, but get in a group for a dungeon and, for all of us not so not so autistically good at games, downright frustrating.
-There is no gui to show buffs/debuffs/hots etc. This may be linked to a greater feeling of "realism" but they do in fact exist in the game, and there is know way to tell unless you enter the character screen and check. This of course does not apply to dots or debuffs on enemies, you just have to have faith they are there.
-The quests are ok the first time around, but try them the second go through and they become so tedious you actually get frustrated.
-The bank tabs require you to quit and re-enter multiple times in order to move items around. This may sound trivial, but it gets really annoying if you forget something or are emailing items from two bank tabs. And the cost to upgrade those tabs is the highest I have seen in games I have played.
-Money generation in the game is very very slow, so slow in fact that you are forced to join trading guilds in order to make any significant amount. This is all well and good I suppose except even that mechanic is based on your luck at finding or salvaging items other people will buy. At higher levels you make more gold, but by then it becomes about tweeking your character, instead of say, buying materials to build sets for leveling.
-The versatility of the crafting system is really good. The major problem with it is that you can't really outfit another character that does not share your item types. For example you create a medium armour character and research all of the intrinsic traits (which could take months btw). If you then create a heavy armour class, by the time you could make them named sets (due to research times) you would level out of the zone and usefulness of the items.
- the majority of the armour sets are ugly or boring, and the modeling for many of the pieces is so bad they just
hang in mid air.
- ***Items purchased from the crown store only apply to the character that purchased it. Thats right, if you want daedric crafting styles for all eight of your characters be ready to shell out $120.... and there are four different crafting styles like this, or five I cant remember.
- It is probably no accident that they are the nicest looking sets in the game.
- The endgame is ridiculous and designed to eliminate the need for zenimax to create more content. I wont say why due to spoilers, but you will get it if you make the mistake of buying this game.
*BUT THE MAIN REASON TO NOT BUY THIS GAME IS THE TERRIBLE CUSTOMER SERVICE*
Allow me to explain. When I first purchased this game it was still subscription based and I did not own a credit card. This was simple enough because it came with a free month of game time. After my purchase I discovered that in order to activate that free game time zenimax required me to link a credit card and they would attempt to bill it to make sure it was good. I sent out an email explaining my situation, and asking why I would need a credit card for free game time. The response took I believe two days to arrive and when it did instead of solving the problem tried to offer other billing solutions. It took quite awhile ( I believe four or five days total ) I finally got a representative to offer me a key that allowed me to play the game on just my free game time. I suppose I should be grateful they did anything at all, but I was now five days behind the friends who bought it with me.
The next blow came quite recently and is the nail in the coffin for me. After reporting an instance where I was constatly falling through the world, I received and email informing me that I had violated the code of conduct in naming my account. There was no recognition of the bug report, no reply to the incident at all, just an emaill that looked very much like a punishment for doubting the zenimax gods. Again, all responses took days to arrive until the final day in which I was told in no uncertain terms that if they decide something that is the way it goes. Period.
This is the short list, there are also inconsistencies in the lore, bad textures, long load times when entering zones and buildings etc etc. I would suggest you read all the reviews here in reference to this game, but keep in mind that depending where you are the price has not come down permanently since launch and the its pretty pricey for a two year old game.

The Elder Scrolls Online: Tamriel Unlimited is an excellent massively multiplayer online game for those who both enjoy other Elder Scrolls games and dislike World of Warcraft.  Although the player should not expect a full Elder Scrolls experience, this game offers a one-of-a-kind multiplayer gameplay experience: fast paced combat, intuitive crafting with a large player-based economy, and a massive amount of diverse locations and quests. Players frustrated with the typical, repetitive nature of modern MMOs will find TESO to be one of the most addicting and entertaining games of 2015.

Combat
Gone are the typical rows of hotkeys that span the width of your computer monitor. Instead, players are given only five hotkeys plus one for an ultimate move per weapon set. This means the player will have to carefully determine the moves they will be able to access for each combat situation. Player versus Player combat is fast-paced and takes place in a massive battleground where players attack and defend against opposing factions.
Economy and Player Interaction
Player-based crafting and economics are also integral parts of TESO. Players can buy and sell their loot and crafted goods through trade guilds, which makes interaction with other players extremely important. Guilds that focus on dungeons or PVP make finding groups for dungeons or raids easy and efficient.
Scale
The title: Tamriel Unlimited, is no understatement. The game features iconic locations from every previous Elder Scrolls release, such as Skyrim and Oblivion; these locations are all included. These iconic locations are also the same size they were in previous games, allowing players endless opportunities to find quests, puzzles, and adventure.
The Elder Scrolls Online offers each player their own personal, long-lasting, and memorable experience. The combat is intense and fast-paced, yet balanced. Player cooperation and interaction is rewarding, yet you could also play through the game solo if you would prefer. The massive world is interactive and complex, so no two players will ever have the same exact experience. I recommend this game to anyone looking for a new and unique gaming adventure that features an engaging story and the best multiplayer gaming experience of 2015.

TL;DR: I really like this game for it's simple yet satisfying gameplay and pretty colors.
This is a very fun game. The game is based around the grappling hook, wing suit and parachute, and these mechanics alone allowed me to sink hours into it. Just flying around is very satisfying and relaxing. The gameplay apart from that is crazy, you blow stuff up in different locations, which pretty much describes the entire game and its plot. The game doesn't take itself serious (only briefly in the end for some reason), and that's what I like about it. It's just one big pile of explosions and flying around.
There's also cool challenges that you can complete around the world. What I liked about these are that they integrate with the massive open world nicely and smoothly. Speaking of the world, it's beautiful and colorful.
The game is not too challenging to complete, although it gets harder when you progress in the story (or by liberating more settlements?). Only when I tried to liberate the central commands had I any chance of dying.
In my eyes the game is perfectly enjoyable, except for a few issues: The game tries to promote the use of vehicles a lot, but there's no reason to use them as flying around is faster and more flexible. I only ever stole jets for blowing up bases more easily. The other more serious flaw with the game is the framerate. I have a decent setup (120 fps in GTA V), but for whatever reason the fps never really reached 60. At times the fps looked like it was capped at 30 too, and dropped frequently during that period. The game could do with some optimization in that aspect.

Although the game is fun during the first of second run. You quickly find out that the entire game is just a grind of collecting resources and food. Once you reach top tier items the gameplay shifts from out and collecting resources to PvP and sitting in your base looking for something to do with all your stuff. PvP in this game is a little unbalanced as some guns are better than others, ammo is too cheap to make causing people with guns willing to kill new spawns because they have the materials to do so all the time. AI in this game is pretty well designed, but not threatning enough once you reach top tier items. Cars are definitely a good feature in the game, because it's an extra step from having good gear to really having good gear. Although they're easy to steal from other people that's fine, because it gives people with low end gear to gain high end gear from other players. The physics with the cars are very fun to play around with and really have no downside, because throughout my time of flipping cars around I have never broken the car or any car parts. Lastly I'd like to cover end game as survival games tend to fail at. This game is a grindfest throughout the whole experience until end game gear. Once you reach that level you have nothing to do else but kill other people. The developers expect people to fight other people just because they can and some do, but there's no point because they won't get anymore gear that they want. Getting C4 is a very frustrating process and is too weak so if you actually successfully raid a base with C4 you won't get anymore in return, because most people protect their bases with multiple layers and walls. I would rate this game a 7/10 for now at the state it is at currently, because it's very addictive and fun for awhile atleast.

Survival Horror, Only In The True Sense Of The Words.
Never in a game have I felt so vulnerable or on edge. The game will make you want to run but doing that comes at a price of death 70% of the time depending on where your runing too. There are guns, ammo is scarce, and shooting at the alien only pisses it off, there are uses for the weapons however and the crafting system lets you create a small aresenal of tools that will help your survival. The game world is expertley detailed and a exact replica of the movies.Small details like the bobbing chickens , sounds that are also straight out of the movies, really help add to the atmosphere and suck you right into it and dosent let go until you either beat the game or give up in utter frustration. The graphics on the game really are quite beautiful , its not some generational leap forward or nothing but it looks darn good with it cranked all the way , going outside the station in some spacewalk mission really lets the games graphics engine shine. The Alien itself is greatley detailed , all that you would expect is here, down to the drool off the aliens teeth.
This is best played on a slow , well thought out approach. You dont have to crouch all the time but you will do a LOT of it and runing while it can be useful, you want to plan such action before hand. The game is a little longer than most, which is a good thing, The unscripted A.I really help bring some the unpredictability out, the "loot" system , if you want to  call it that , is all random and varies from game to game or save to save, same with the A.I. All in all , if your fan of the Alien movies, then this is the game for you. Turn your lights out, sound up and see for yourself, you will be ashamed of yourself of all the jumping in your seat that you will end up doing. Please though, remember, this is NOT A FAST PAACED FPS, Its not meant to be played in that manner, its not Battlefield, Call of Duty etc and playing it as such will get you killed over and over again, so save yourself the frustration and DONT DO IT!
All in ALL Im going to give the game a 9.0 / 10

You gotta know what you're getting into if you pick up something like Euro Truck Simulator. It's a simulation game of exactly that. Driving a truck around Europe. You pick up cargo. Drive across highways, and drop it off in other places. That's it. However, if you're like me, and a life on the open road has been something you've fantasized about, or if you're one of those weird people who (like me) actually enjoy driving and going on long road trips, this game can be very relaxing.
There's an economic aspect to it, in the sense that you're trying to complete jobs to earn money to grow your trucking business, and because of the DLC, there's a lot of customization options available once you get to the point where you're kitting out your own trucks.
But if you're expecting anything really in-depth, it's not here, and if any of this sounded boring or pointless to you, this isn't the game for you.
However, for the type of gamer who's just looking to relax and would like to be able to have a beer while driving, without doing it in real life. This is the game for you.
