This is a uniquely terrifying and captivating game to play. Steam tells me that I have about 88 hours clocked on this game and I have completed all 50 of the achievements, so I should be able to write this with a fairly expansive overview.
Fans of survival horror are likely to enjoy this, but the people really in for a treat are fans of the original 1979 Ridley Scott film 'Alien'. On a visual level, this game is simply gorgeous. Every grimy aspect of the film's 'truckers in deep space' art and set design is faithfully recreated in painstaking detail. The retro fonts on the computers, the bulbous tubes and wires of the corridors, the flickering lights, the seeping mist from every crevice. It is stunning to behold for your first hour or so of gameplay before you are gripped with terror.
Likewise, the sound design is impeccable. Monitor beeps, the sounds of doors opening and closing, echoes through the long corridors; these all combine to create a truly claustrophobic atmosphere. Many other aspects of the sound design are made to sound similar to the soon familiar sounds of the Alien creature itself, making you wonder if you simply are hearing things or about to have a sharp tail jam through your torso from behind you. Add this to the fact that Jerry Goldsmith's original haunting orchestral score is put to good use, and you have one bloody terrifying atmosphere.
Another big plus for the game is the Alien itself. It is actually scary once again, after a long period of simply being cannon fodder in more recent films and games like 'Aliens: Colonial Marines'. Much has been made of the Alien's AI, and this works massively in the game's favour. The unpredictablilty of the Alien makes a huge case for replayability and it never truly stops being terrifying. Even when you don't SEE the Alien, it is never truly out of your mind. You hear it rustling in the vents. Whilst creeping down a corridor, you notice with terror the slowly dripping saliva of the Alien from an overhead duct, waiting to pounce on you. The easier diifficulties go fairly gentle on the player, but hard difficulty is where this AI is shown at its best. Nowhere is truly safe and you genuinely feel as if you are being hunted.
The game is not without its flaws. The story, whilst still being gripping enough, will not come with any real suprises to fans familiar with the franchise. The game is also just a tad too long to fully sustain the neccessary terror for its material. It's the equivalent of if the original film had been 3 hours rather than 2; the audience would begin to shift a little in their seats, rather than being truly terrified for a solid entirety.
Regardless of that however, this game has a unique sense of dread about it and is in many ways the game which Alien fans have been pining for. A fitting tribute to the horrors of the original film and scary in its own right and its own medium.

Slime Rancher is one of the greatest games I have ever played, It is simple, calming and filled with life. To start it has an incredible soundtrack, one of the best on steam. Slime Rancher is a beautiful success story for Early Access, and it is exciting to see this game leave for 1.0 release.
There's parts of this game that will appeal to almost anyone. There's a lot of humour with the slimes and their behaviour. There's the seemingly endless search for treasure pods. There's a relentless economic game of gathering and selling resources to a market. And there is an astounding amount of detail and love that went into crafting all of the regions and environments here. With each update I didn't think they could make the game even more fun to play and yet somehow they managed just that.
Looking forward to watching this game continue to grow (they've already laid out the next few updates in their roadmap).

I just noticed I never wrote a review for this game-- sorry for that, Nick! I was reminded by the release trailer for the game that just came out (Wow, Beatrix looks great!)
I've seen friends and strangers both refer to the game as "like Stardew Valley, but X." The truth is, you just can't compare this game to anything else.
Slime Rancher may be shipped as a farming game, even in the title-- "Rancher". But this isn't a mere farming game. It's a work of art. Each area is hand-crafted with care and attention down to the tips of the pink grass. The beauty is even preserved on low graphics settings, which is good news for this old junky vegetable of mine. Did I mention it runs relatively well on said junky vegetable?
I could go on and on, but I can't. I can't put it into words. This game leaves me unable to think of just what to say to do it justice.
...It has slime basketball with music that sounds like it's from a boss level in a Korean MMO? I guess?
You'll get gang-attacked from behind by suicide bombing slimes while hunting for the last fairy slime you need for your collection?
You'll tear your hair out trying to create Slime Science gadgets but remember they're all totally optional?
You'll nearly drift off to sleep wrapped up in a blanket on a cold morning while listening to the water slimes make purring noises and then be confused why the cat slimes don't make purring noises?
You'll question your morality as you throw elderly chickens into an incinerator to turn them into fresh ash for your firey slimes to burn as fuel?
You'll suck up 50 slimes and shoot them into the air to watch them fall down and bounce?
You'll come back to a ranch of starving cat-slimes after a night out and watch them all leap into the stars as you fire a single carrot into the air?
You'll wonder why there are a bunch of sealed doors when an old man had already explored the entire ranch and come to the conclusion he was a master speedrunner that used a jetpack to fly over everything?
...You'll make memories with this game, alright. I don't buy many games that are above $10, but this one was definitely worth it.

As of Patch 14 Beta which many, myself included, consider to have done the most significant improvements to sieges so far, Rome II is in a very playable, fun, decently optimized and in mostly balanced state.
I would strongly suggest NOT considering reviews of this game that are old and did not review the game in its current state, like Angry Joe's review of the game. At the time of the review he was right and I certainly agreed with him, but the game has changed very much and for the better since then.

This is quite a realistic zombie apocolypse game. The rules are simple. Stay alive, finish the objective, conserve ammo, cooperate and not to get infected. In such a game where everything plays an important roles, everyone need to master a certain level of skills to survive.
I enjoy the game due to some of its realistic approach. However, I need to touch on a few important points of this game.
1) Infection. Players must try to survive and avoid getting attacked by zombies as much as they can. There is a chance that every hit from zombies will infect you even if you are at full health. Pills will only delay the effect for 3 minutes before players began to experience transformation. Suiciding is a choice which some players made to keep their companions from risk of getting mauled by a teammate turned zombies.
2) Ammo are rare and players must learn to conserve them or not to hold onto all the ammo. Face with uncertainty and greedy teammates who might take everything and leaving you with nothing, your every bullets used or conserve might determine your life and death.
3) Cooperation. It is essentially the main theme in this game. Having more teammates doesn't mean you will have greater chance of surviving. Yet, only those who possess skills and good cooperation will most likely get out alive.
4) Objectives. The objective maps have various objectives required to be completed. However, it doesn't actually get highlighted unless you come close to the object and it is hard for newcomers to know what to do. For an early access title, this game is nothing short of incredible.
I played Black Mesa back when it still a mod rather than a fully-fledged title on Steam (granted, it was in the process of getting through the stages of Steam Greenlight, but still), and looking at the changes made in the Steam version are a major improvement. That's not to say that the mod version was bad by any means; it was actually really good, and was an exceedingly ambitious mod that people had talked about, but no one had the stones to step up and actually commit to.
The models have all been refurbished and given great looking animations, the level design has been polished, and multiplayer was added, and is just damn fun to play.
The one thing that threw me off when playing this is the fact that the singleplayer combat can be a bit difficult sometimes (the marines seem to just always hit you), and the game seems to require the movements and agility that the GoldSrc engine was so well know for, yet, because it's built on the Source engine, it FEELS like Half-Life 2 movement and actions. That's not necessarily a bad thing, but it's definitely something that threw me off when I first began playing it.
Also, from what I've been able to gather, the developement team is really well involved in the community and the game, which is something that I've come to admire of certain indie devs/mod devs. In fact, just earlier today, I played a multiplayer match with several other people, one of which was a level designer for this game. He seemed really friendly, and was actually really open to casually tossed criticism. In fact, he even went so far as to make self-deprecating quips about some of the maps he designed.
When a developer is not only open and patient with people's opinions, but able to casually joke about their product's shortcomings and fully acknowledge that their game is just as beautifully imperfect as any other game, that's a sign of nothing short of a great developer.
Anyone who's ever been a fan of Half-Life, or just of great mods that blossomed into full-blown ongoing professional products, for the love of GabeN, buy this game. You'd be doing the devs and the community a huge favor.

First the graphics were good but not as impressive as I expected. For example I was surprised to see a 2D image of the space station in an opening sequence.
-----The cinematic music was faithful to the original films and was a very nice touch. There is a generous amount of ambience, which is something that is really important to me.
-----The alien death Sequences were intense. However being killed by the Alien just became routine because it killed me so much.
-----The game featured a lot of darkness I was very impressed by this. Lighting was a strong point.
-----The alien looked good, it moved very fluidly and was very convincing. It was nerve racking when it was Stomping around just centimetres away from my hiding spots. Detailed closeups of characters during dialogue and cutscenes also looked pretty good.
-----The Sci-Fi world was faithful to the original film and period. It was the ‘future of the 80’s’. I was very happy to see a retro style world which didn’t try to look cute or goofy. One of the most impressive yet slow and uneventful sections was the space-walk on the space station exterior. There were massive satellite dishes and the you could get a good view of the station’s colossal towers.
I had a very confused introduction to combat. I thought stealth would be the only solution to hostile encounters. I spent an hour or so of my time playing the game not making any progress until I figured this out.
-----Next thing, save stations sometimes didn’t seem to feature frequently enough or sometimes I would miss them completely. The autosave feature didn’t always work at logical points in the game. After dying which happened frequently, I could find myself losing 15 minutes or more of gameplay. Plus I often had to repeat tasks and uneventful sequences again and again which became tedious as cool as they were.
-----Being able to save manually at any time could have been used to avoid this. Many things which I had to repeat in the game just weren’t necessary. Meaning that I spent comparatively less time engaging in more interesting action
-----Gunplay is actually very jerky in this game. Guns are hard to use accurately and fire very slowly. You have no access to automatic weaponry at all. Most weapons are rudimentary or makeshift. You will not feel like a badass marine or one woman army. You are very vulnerable. This was a very strong aspect to the the gameplay experience
-----The Alien lurks in many sections of the game. You can’t kill it. But if it get’s a hold of you it will kill you instantly, and it did so to me frequently.
-----Some items will cause it to retreat for a short time. But your supplies are very limited. For the most part you must hide and sneak around it. Being able to duck under furniture was a very cool way to do this.
-----The alien’s movement patterns were very unpredictable. When it’s gone and I thought it was safe to come out, it would often re-appear suddenly and unexpectedly. Graphics aside the Alien A.I. was the best and most important feature of the game.
-----Dealing with the Alien was very challenging and intense. The section which first really featured the alien would only take a few minutes to walk through if it wasn’t present. However because of my frequent deaths it took me around an hour to get through. For this reason sometimes long sections featuring the Alien could actually become tiresome.
-----But there are occasionally stages where the Alien is not present. This was a welcome change of pace.
-----The other main adversaries are the working Joe androids. They are very tough. But they’re very slow and even large groups of them can be easily dispatched without taking a scratch. However they can be very unnerving if you’re in a confined area and several of them are converging on you.
It took me around 20 hours to complete Alien: Isolation in the hardest difficulty. I think that was too long. I would have been happier to get through the main storyline in only half that time. Because I feel that I often found myself in the same situation repeatedly only in different places.
-----Also the ending wasn’t conclusive. I don’t think any full game should end with what is essentially a teaser.
-----But I still enjoyed it overall. It’s an extremely impressive Alien game. It was really satisfying to have a game in the franchise that wasn’t a massive disappointment, it’s really done it justice.

SMITE is an amazingly good game.
Me and a friend have been since before it came on Steam, and it's still really good. As of the time of this review, I've put just under 200 hours and I've only really played 3 gods. If you're someone who gets bored easily with more or less the same gameplay, you'll want to play way more than that by then.
There's a rotation of gods free each week, or you can pay to unlock all the gods, forever, even new gods added. It's not pay-to-win at all. You can pay to unlock skins (cosmetics), or you CAN buy gems to unlock gods or grind favor. However, you do start with a few gods unlocked at the beginning, so odds are you can have fun with them in the mean time.
One of the coolest things about smite is: It's a 3rd person MOBA.
I tried Dota 2, and I really didn't like it. I didn't even want to try LoL, mainly because I just don't like MOBAs. Smite however, doesn't feel like one. 3rd person, and WASD to move makes it a lot more unique, and a lot more fun.
There's 5 gamemodes. Joust (3v3), Siege (4v4), Arena (5v5), Conquest (5v5) and the MOTD, which is random each day.
All in all, this is a really fun game. It requires a separate account from Steam, which is really the only downside I can think of, but even then it's not a big deal. It's free, so why not give it a try?
EDIT: Steam version no longer works properly for me (and they've stated they're aware of this issue) but I still recommend getting this from their website, and using the standalone launcher!

Total War Rome 2 is without a doubt the worst game in the series, maybe on par with Empire. Thankfully however this isn't saying too much as it is a pretty decent strategy game. It's definitely still not worth 60 dollars. To cut the review short, I'll do the standard pro/con list most people do.
Pros:
+ When the AI or other units don't bug out battles can be immensely fun.
+ Multiplayer campaign and multiplayer battles are very fun with friends, although public games are few and relatively boring.
+ Graphics are very good, but still not as good as Shogun 2.
+ Units are very diverse and different cultures have different tactics (Romans depend on raw discipline and heavy infantry, Carthaginians are flexible using different soldiers from different cultures, Celts and Germanics use the very shock and fear of a powerful charge, etc.)
+ New province/region system is better than what we had with Empire and Napoleon.
+ Modding community is very good.
Cons:
- AI is very stupid in battles and are very incompetent when managing an empire.
- Looking at soldiers fight is very boring and poorly presented (They often flick off into the air and spin around when getting poked in the♥♥♥♥♥♥ etc.)
- DLC Campaigns are very uninteresting with the exception of the Greek DLC and the free one with Emperor Edition.
- Many, Many Faction pack DLC's and other ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t.
- Despite what the major Review companies say the "Super epic Rome 2 cavalry charges!" is nothing more than Celtic Riders running over the first line of soldiers and then slapping at the poor ♥♥♥♥ers below before getting shoved off their horse by a shield.
- Too many factions that have little to no different besides faction bonuses. There are really only about 5 different unit rosters.
- Most special units are just things like oathsworn (Celts with chainmail, a sword, and oval shield) and greek hoplites with pretty shields and shiny helmets.
- Tech tree is pretty standard and boring.
- Often times the major nations like Rome get taken over by Etruscans or some miniscule Celtic tribe.
- Naval battles are pointless, boring, hard to command and this is where the AI bugs out the most.
- I know this isn't really a negative spot on gameplay but the majority of the budget went to bribing IGN and making "Super early pre-alpha footage" look nice. Just look at the Carthage siege "pre-alpha" video and then watch release footage and you will see what I mean.
- Hard to run without a high-end computer.
- AI really bad at sieges and there are only about 1 walled city in every region or so, making most assaults boring.

There is always going to be that traditional balance between "publish now!" and "work the bugs out!" among the Total War fan base... TW:Rome II admirably gave the fans what they wanted, while not only overcoming the issues but improving upon the game itself.  The result is a highly playable game that differs from previous TW franchise games, but is perfectly suited for the timeframe.
For those who have never introduced themselves to the Total War series, you're in for a visual treat.  The game itself is beautiful.  The gameplay?  Nowhere near the steep learning curve of some of the other games such as the Europa Universalis series, nor is the gameplay on par with the Civilization or other hex-and-counter type games.  Give yourself an evening or two and walk yourself through the tutorials.  It's worth it.
Those of us who are used to the TW series, I am one of those who enjoys the differences between the TW games (and am unashamedly a fan of Empire: Total War and would love to see a Renaissance period that caputred 1300-1700... shameless plug).  There is a difference between Shogun II and Napoleon and Empire, but don't let that bog you down.  If you love this time period of history, you will not be disappointed.
Playing through the factions, one does get the sense that history could have gone very differently -- the styles of combat are different, different tactics and strategies must be employed, you feel the very real lack of archers (if you are the Romans) and love the very real impact of ballista (if you are the Romans).  The Carthaginian elephants are a beautiful thing to see charge into a packed line of Roman legionaires.  Greek phalanx vs. Mithridatic cavalry.  The barbarians of Gaul swarming over a hill with fireballs leading the way?  Oh yes... this can be yours...

I played the mod some time ago and waited for a sale before buying the steam version. Seems I was correct since these two don't differ much at first glance. Xen is still missing, how long has it been now? I understand the devs wanting Xen to be perfect, but 3 years and counting come on..
Personal issues aside, if you love half life as much as me this mod/game is a must play. The level design is beautifull, with every original level recreated in source with lovelingly attention to detail. The sound is great, the music is great, the weapons and animations feel like those of the original game. I especially love the moment where you pick up the alien hivegun and I'm sure you will too.
Some of the places that weren't very clear objectivewise in the original game, have been improved. I remember not finding the fuel and such in blast pit, alot more clear now. Also less 'interesting' levels like residue processing, with the conveyer belts maze actually look like a functioning facility now instead of an excuse to go platform jumping. Every level has believable paths and doors ( some of them closed obviously ) so that it actually feels like a huge facility people work in ( or used too :p ). The puzzles have been improved here and there as well and powering up the generator ( I think blast pit ? ) is no longer a strange deathtrap, which improves the immersion immensely.
If I had to name a couple of downsides, the difficulty curve can be very random. One section you're blazing through, the other you reload 10 - 20 times because you have 20 health and those alien grunts instagib you in a second. Usually the health pack placement is good, excellent even. But I've had times where I was swimming in health but didn't need it, others I was begging the game for a healthkit but had to retry 10 times to headshot a marine 200 yards away that kept instakilling me. Health and hev suit power drains FAST in Black mesa and it's a good thing. Just be prepared to die more then in your average modern fps game, that's coming from a guy playing on normal.
Also sometimes AI would get 'stuck' for no apparent reason. For instance a vortigaunt or marine would see me, start shooting. I would duck into cover, after peeking out again they did not do anything untill I shot at them. This made some encounters a little too easy and it has to be a bug, but one I did not remember from the modversion.
Charging AI was also a downside sometimes, especially for the marines. I'm hoping to see them patched to stay in cover a bit more. They are absolutely lethal aimwise and the charging shotgun marines are especially deadly. But I saw one of them leave his mg to rush me for instance, which isn't exactly tactical. More grenade usage would be nice to see as well. The charge behavior worked well on the alien soldiers though, I had them smack me to death a couple of times.
To sum it up:
+absolutely beautifull recreation of half life
+great sound/music
+plenty of content
+epic feeling of nostalgia
+deadly marines
+marines talk like actual people
-marine AI could use a little tweaking still
-difficulty fluctuates, although annoying not that bad because of quicksave.
-AI sometimes not working? ( standing still, ignoring the player, one time an npc got stuck on a wall )
-marines talk like actual people
-still no Xen
nitpicks:
-shotgun reload animation seems a little slow and hard to interrupt ( I stopped using it mostly because of the rushing marines killing me whilst cocking it ) Make it a more effective but with less ammo.
-vortigaunts no longer one shot kill with magnum unless headshot ( they are hunched so alot of times you miss the head, especially annoying in the lambda reactor level )
Should you buy this, I think so. If you already played the mod wait for a sale like I did. Now let's hope they fix the last bugs and add Xen before the next century. Also devs, please add back the surface tension section where the marine drops the satchel in the tunnel, it was one of my favourite half life moments.
Despite my nagging, it's a great experience and every half life fan should play this.

System Shock 2 really is one of the best games ever made.  It's one of those games where all the elements mesh together so well that it still manages to be a great game 10+ years after release.  There are graphic mods available which I highly recommend (check the game hub for a guide) though they definitely aren't necessary to enjoy the game.
The gameplay is a mesh of FPS and RPG similar to Deus Ex, though gun accuracy does not suffer due to a low skill level.  Many objects are interactible and you will need to utilize mouse interfaces quite often.  One unique thing about the game is that it does not pause when interacting so you need to be aware of your surroundings so you are not attacked while doing so.
The game uses the old-school style of giving you objectives without marking exactly where they are so you need to pay attention to where you're going and what you're doing.  The one thing I wish the game had was markers on the map for mission locations once you discover them as it can be difficult to find them again when you need them.
There is a good variety of weapons for melee, ranged, and psi combat.  The guns are very accurate unlike Deus Ex, though the recoil can throw off your aim.  Melee combat is definitely a weak spot in the game with the range and hitbox being very short and unclear, as well as the melee attacks being quite slow.  There is an overhead attack upgrade you can get that unfortunately makes these problems worse.
Where the game really shines is in the atmosphere, writing, and of course, SHODAN.  Even with the very dated graphics, this game manages to be the creepiest game I have ever played.  I admit I have not yet played Amnesia, but I do believe System Shock 2 could give it a run for its money.  SHODAN is an amazing character, and really adds to that atmosphere as well.
About the game difficulty: I've heard many people say the game is too hard.  I didn't have much trouble though I am very experienced with FPS's.  I do know that psi builds are very difficult compared to others.  Total completion time: ~12 hours.
Play this game!  You will not regret it.

Amazing game. There are obviously many parralels to Bioshock given that they have the same developers and similar horror-esque gameplay. SS2's gameplay feels smoother than that of Bioshock and the interface is much better than Bioshock's. Both games involve rationing limited ammo supply, which adds to the horror feel. SS2 can be rather unforgiving, so I recommend saving frequently. Graphics look dated of course, so I recommend doing some modding before getting started. I found a lot of good ones in this thread:
The gameplay is much more complex than Bioshock's, with a variety of different skills which you can spend your resources in and multiple types of ammo for many weapons. This allows for much customization in the way you want to play and strategizing in deciding what ammo to use against what enemies. The tetris-like inventory system is something you don't often see anymore, but it added a certain amount of challenge to deciding what items to keep and which to leave behind. The story is longer than I had expected; there is a good 20-25 hours of gameplay if you go at the speed I went at (I didn't rush). The ending is awesome, I wish there were a sequel. A couple things I would change: It would be helpful if the game paused when you had the inventory open; it's annoying when an enemy finds you while you are moving items around. The hacking is simple and boring, Bioshock's is far superior. Some of the voice acting is pretty cheesy, especially for the minor characters, but most of it is fine. I like the option of waiting to listen to audio logs rather than being forced to listen to them immediately after picking them up. This allows you to get out of combat so you can play closer attention, or wait until other audio you are listening to has stopped. Bioshock doesn't have this option. Bioshock also got rid of leaning, which is a cool and helpful mechanic. Conclusion: SS2 is like Bioshock except it's in space, more complex, designed for PC, has better gameplay, and has worse graphics (which can be remedied by mods). Awesome game. 9/10.

With the main setting in space on a ship that has been through everything you can imagine, there are several sectors that you will get to explore, very nice level design, and sound that goes along great with the enviornments of the game. Shock 2 also has a nice RPG element to it, with three classes to master, which are the Psychic, Soldier, and Hacker. These classes come in handy in situations from fighting enemies to outsmarting complex security systems. The game's story is nice too, with some twists that will leave you astounded, and an interesting back story that will keep you wanting more. With all of this in one game, i would say the only real flaw is the textures of the characters and levels. However, this is a minor flaw at that, and with everything else to make up for it (and considering the time it was made), this game is a must-have for survival-horror fans and shooter fans alike.
If you like Bioshock and want to look at the game that inspired it, look no further this is the game for you.

Just finished this.  Maybe endured is the better word.  This game is grueling.  Don't get me wrong.  It's grueling in an amazing and breathtaking way but the experience is so immersive, you'll be leaping at every beep from your motion tracker.
This game inspires dread.  It is a masterpiece of tension.  It understands its source material (the original 1979 Alien) and executes its vision of the future flawlessly.  The game integrates into Alien lore seamlessly, taking place in the time span between Ellen Ripley's first and second encounters with the xenomorph.  Since Amanda Ripley lives out her entire adult life in that timeframe between when Ellen Ripley sets out with the Nostromo and when her lifeboat is recovered, the devs have a great window to weave the tale they desire.  The player character - Ripley's daughter, Amanda - works for good old Weyland-Yutani 15 years after her mother's disapperance but hasn't completely let go of the incident.  When a low-level executive named Christopher Samuels shows up with news of the recovery of the Nostromo's flight recorder, Ripley finds herself unable to pass up the opportunity for some closure on the matter.  The recorder turned up with a salvage recovery team at the run-down, nearly decommissioned space station, Sevastopol.
The game takes a few nods from the sequel, Aliens, as well, and the arrival at Sevastopol station is met with silence.  It wouldn't be a survival horror in space if the boarding didn't go awry.  You enter Sevastopol, mostly unscathed, to find a state of anarchy, bedlam, and the oh-so-popular breakdown of society, whereupon you attempt to deal with one crisis after the next while unraveling the mystery of what happened to Ellen Ripley - all the while fending off paranoid, trigger-happy survivors, the creepy budget-conscious Seegson corporation android workers who are operating on an unknown agenda, and, of course, the eponymous xenomorph.
Unlike every entry into the Aliens Vs. Predator series, the alien is not some spooky but fragile cannon fodder to be mowed down in the hundreds.  It seems Creative Assembly and Sega were all too keen to distance themselves from the negative opinion surrounding Colonial Marines and focused on recreating the terror of the original film.  You'll be provided weapons, yet you won't want to use them.  Such as it is, weapon use creates an abundance of noise which broadcasts to the Alien what part of the station dinner will be served in.  Stealth is the focus here and you'll be well-served by ducking behind the nearest upturned table or hiding in a nearby locker.  The game provides you the means to create diversions to divert your human, android, and xenomorph pursuers though the AI of the xenomorph is prone to learning from your tricks if you overutilize them.  On top of this, the xenomorph and to a lesser extent, humans and androids display a fantastic randomness to their actions.  Humans will establish a vague patrol whilst scavenging supplies but the xenomorph, being the apex predator in this environment, will freely roam, stop, investigate and double back, seemingly on a whim creating for some truly terrifying cat-and-mouse mechanics.  You cannot kill the alien with your improvised weaponry.  You can only distract it or at best buy yourself a momentary respite.   But rest assured, the thing will be back sooner than you'd prefer.
You'll hide, you'll freeze, you'll stare at your motion tracker trying to figure out where the thing is.  You'll listen to it stomp around.  You'll listen to it thump through the air vents.  You'll stare at every open ceiling vent as you walk under it, terrified a jet-black claw will lunge out and drag you to an inglorious doom.  Some purists may take issue with the fact that the xenomorph isn't particularly stealthy (clever though it may be).  They're taking issue with the fact that the drone in the original Alien was primarily an ambush predator, moving silently, keeping to inaccessible areas.  They do have a point, but the xenomorph in Isolation is much older, having been aboard Sevastopol for a month or so and has had time to break down social order to where there is no real resistance to its ability to operate.  The crew in Alien were dealing with something less than a few days old, which did not have any understanding of humanity and was facing a crew united towards it's destruction.  The crew of Sevastopol certainly has no love for the xenomorph but they are already quite busy killing each other over supplies, evading the ever-present synthetic workforce, and trying to regain contact with civilization beyond the station.  In short, they are divided, broken and terrified and the drone no longer needs to fear moving amongst their dwindling numbers.
Alien: Isolation offers a fantastic simulation of surviving a grueling experience being constantly hunted by one of fiction's greatest terrors that is immersive and fleshes out more of the Alien universe.  It was delightful seeing a rival competing company - Seegson - take the primary role in place of Weyland-Yutani.  WY does have their hand to play in the matter but given the movies' borderline obsessiveness with 'the Company', you'd think they were the only brand in the universe.  A word of warning, it's a very intense game and also a very long one - perhaps artificially so, as there is a great deal of back-tracking.  But in the context of this game, I feel it fits.  There's a lot of backtracking in the films and a lot of moving from one crisis to the next and constantly dreading the appearance of the xenomorph the entire way.  It's what makes the franchise so tense to begin with.  And I for one, welcome the length, as I find far too many games are all too quick to run through the narrative with no regards to pacing or experience and this is a game that feels like a marathon.  If you're looking for a cool sci-fi horror to pulse-rifle your way through in 5 hours, keep shopping.  If you're ready for a 12-20+ hour endeavor fraught with suspense and heart-pounding adrenaline as your pursuer passes within arm's length of you, this is for you.
There are the occasional issues but you'll be hard-pressed to find a game that understands its franchise so well and legitimately terrifies you.
Graphics: 9/10 - beautiful lighting and environment, slightly iffy human models, weird cutscene human models that have this odd perma-sweat going.  Not really going to knock off points for something that plays so small a role in the overall visual presentation.  It's a beautiful game, with lovely contrast between the boxy 80's style retro-future electronics and the breathtaking views of the station and surrounding space.
Sound: 10/10 - I really can't think of anything I'd fault with the audio.  This game is great with surround sound, helping you locate where your nemesis is without seeing it.  There is a healthy balance of tense silence (broken up with Amanda's footfalls on the deck and the occasional bleep from the motion tracker), and dramatic string-heavy composition when a pursuer is seeking you.  It reaches unnerving crescendos when they close or when the narrative action is rising.  Voice acting is decent to good, though not a huge presense in the game.  Props to the devs for getting hold of Sigourney Weaver, Tom Skerritt, Harry Dean Stanton, Veronica Cartwright, and Yaphet Kotto to reprise their roles from the 1979 film for some additional audio logs recovered from the Nostromo.
Story: 6/10 - Arguably the weakest aspect of the experience, though it's still decent in my opinion.  Characters don't receive a ton of time to develop since you'll spend most of the game removed from them or only in sporadic radio contact.  The story is a bit traveled and it's a little bit of a stretch on some things.  Still acceptable though
Overall, I'd say it's a 9/10 and a fantastic example of survival horror gaming.

I have to say, this game did not have a good start. the Mouse sensitivity was tied to the fps, and the fps was as bad a 6 month old cheese left in the sun and marinated with trash for 50 years ago. I was so disappointed in the proformance I almost returned the game... almost. Now there is a beta patch out that has fixed most of the problems I experienced while playing. Thats not to say that its all peachy good, heres a list of the problems so you know what your dealing with with the beta patch.
-The framerate constantly jumps between 60 and 30, but rarely goes below 30 (oddly enough, enabling V-sync improves the proformance dramatically)
-They have lowered the power of the AA and reduced the draw distance on all settinging in order to game proformance
-Dynamic Resolution does improve the frame rate, but will often make the game look blury, even when set to prefer quality.
That is all I have found, there is still a need for improvments, but it is very playable now.
My thoughts of why it is so poorly optimized:
It is the Void engine and the new art style. the original Dishonored had closed cell graphics with no black lines, definantly not the prettiest style, but it gave good proformance. It was made on the unreal engine, a well optimized and well known engine. The void engine however strides to more realistic visuals, with heavy detail and natural animations, and don't get me wrong, the engine is beautiful, the art style switch is brilliant, but the Void engine is brand new, and new things are always clunky and inefficient.
I would recommend buying this game, not now, but after the release of the 1.2 patch, the gameplay is amazing, the mechanics are awesome, and the story is good. So be patient, I mean just look at Batman, a fantastic game AFTER it was fixed.

Im reading other reveiws talking about how the game is "unplayable" due to low FPS and no optimization yet i was able to run through the entire game with High Chaos on "very high" graphics clocking an easy 60 FPS. My performance was just fine and  it was beautiful.
The game takes place about 15 years after the original Dishonored (which i would reccomend you play first just so you're filled in on the back story) and it does a very nice job filling in the in-between space as you go through the game. Im not going to spoil any of the story in this review because i strongly reccomend you experience it yourself and have an amazing time with it like i did. My high chaos play-through took about 12 hours and I estimate a low chaos to hover anywhere around 20-25 hours so the length is fairly good.
The new powers are pretty great and the upgrading system for them has gone more in depth since the previous game which i really liked a lot. Most powers now have 2 branches you can upgrade and, hunting for all of the runes in the levels, I found it pretty easy to form a play style I was most comfortable with in the gameplay. For example, you can upgrade the grip ability to grab humans so what I would do is hide in the up in the rafters and pull bad guys up with it and assassinate them up there.
Bethesda has also introduced a new enemy to the series in this installment of Dishonored: The clockwork robots. And let me tell you, these robots can be nothing but terrifying when you first encounter them and don't really know how to deal with them effectively. The first level where they were introduced was just a blast because it seemed like the perfect about of these guys in the whole level. But after this first level it kind of dissapointed me that I only saw about 5 in the rest of the game after that because there would be some spots in there where they would be perfect.
The stealth in this game is a lot like the previous game
and for Dishonored veterans like me, it will be very easy to pick up on quickly. It just feels easy to be able to hide up in the rafters and evade enemies.
Combat is not something i had to deal with much because i was trying to stay stealthy but in the moments i did encounter it, it was very fluent and seemed well done. Though like Dishonored you have guys who will stand about 10 feet away from you and shoot at you, this doesn't seem to happen as often which is an improvement. The swordplay is alright but it seems harder to block now.
Overall i would strongly reccomend this game because it feels good running and is very fun. If you do notice framerate issues with low graphics maybe try getting it for a console instead of PC because this was an amazing experience for any dishonored fan.

I'm not a true Call of Duty fan. I played the first two as well as Modern Warfare, but mostly fell off after that. I've also never been into competitive multiplayer. Despite that, I enjoyed my time with Advanced Warfare. The storyline was a little goofy at parts, but the characters were genuinely well-realized at times. Some of the motion capture was off here-and-there, but there were other instances when character animations were quite impressive. Graphics are as expected for this series - which is to say very competent and mostly polished.
The multiplayer was a surprising lot of fun for me. I enjoyed the macro game of leveling up gear and eventually prestiging and doing it all again. There's not a lot of sense to it, but the compulsion is fun (personal opinion, as is all of this). That said, the community can be a little rough at times. There is some hyper-competitive hatred as seen in many modern competitive games. It's hard to play too long without someone calling "Hax" and generally downplaying the lovable characteristics of your mother... But the community also has some bright spots and chat is easily ignored if you find yourself in a tough crowd.
If you play FPS games for the storyline, you could certainly do worse than Advanced Warfare. The action is exciting and the characters provide some memorable moments. If you enjoy the competitive scene and find incentive in the sort of gear-grinding CoD is famous for, then you might really have fun here. If you have and always will disdain the Call of Duty series, this probably won't change your mind.

There is always going to be that traditional balance between "publish now!" and "work the bugs out!" among the Total War fan base... TW:Rome II admirably gave the fans what they wanted, while not only overcoming the issues but improving upon the game itself.  The result is a highly playable game that differs from previous TW franchise games, but is perfectly suited for the timeframe.
For those who have never introduced themselves to the Total War series, you're in for a visual treat.  The game itself is beautiful.  The gameplay?  Nowhere near the steep learning curve of some of the other games such as the Europa Universalis series, nor is the gameplay on par with the Civilization or other hex-and-counter type games.  Give yourself an evening or two and walk yourself through the tutorials.  It's worth it.
Those of us who are used to the TW series, I am one of those who enjoys the differences between the TW games (and am unashamedly a fan of Empire: Total War and would love to see a Renaissance period that caputred 1300-1700... shameless plug).  There is a difference between Shogun II and Napoleon and Empire, but don't let that bog you down.  If you love this time period of history, you will not be disappointed.
Playing through the factions, one does get the sense that history could have gone very differently -- the styles of combat are different, different tactics and strategies must be employed, you feel the very real lack of archers (if you are the Romans) and love the very real impact of ballista (if you are the Romans).  The Carthaginian elephants are a beautiful thing to see charge into a packed line of Roman legionaires.  Greek phalanx vs. Mithridatic cavalry.  The barbarians of Gaul swarming over a hill with fireballs leading the way?  Oh yes... this can be yours...
Very simply, I learned to love the exploding catapult, or bomb as it were.  If you love the Total War series, love the time period, or simply want to introduce yourself to an excellent wargame -- Iacta aleae! (Throw the dice!)

It's a good game.  It has its flaws, but overall it's with worth playing.
First of all it's a survival game, so you're underequipped most of the time.
It's focused on atmosphere and the experience of being challenged more than it is about action itself. If you're looking for action you're better off with L4D2. This is much more than just an action game.
Single zombies are usually fairly easy to handle (if you have a melee weapon or a gun). Large groups can be challenging, especially because you run out of ammo and stamina quickly.
One silly thing is that in scenario modes there are spawn points for zombies (often in rooms with no windows and one entrance), so at times you will find yourself attacked from behind by a randomly spawned zombie just after you had cleared a certain area or part of a building. This can seriously ruin the mood.
Sometimes the game is kind of cryptic, and requires you to use very specific items for certain tasks, while at other times virtually any item will do (a good example is having to use a chainsaw to cut through planks in the attic, while being able to pry them off in almost all other areas in game).
Online multiplayer is what ruins the game (at least for me it does). While single-player and LAN games are indeed fun and entertaining, playing with random people might ruin the game for you. You will come across people making fart sounds on voice channel and killing you for ammo and resources. The devs give you no tools to deal with that other than leaving the game and joining another one with hopes of a better outcome.

Im reading other reveiws talking about how the game is "unplayable" due to low FPS and no optimization yet i was able to run through the entire game with High Chaos on "very high" graphics clocking an easy 60 FPS. My performance was just fine and  it was beautiful.
The game takes place about 15 years after the original Dishonored (which i would reccomend you play first just so you're filled in on the back story) and it does a very nice job filling in the in-between space as you go through the game. Im not going to spoil any of the story in this review because i strongly reccomend you experience it yourself and have an amazing time with it like i did. My high chaos play-through took about 12 hours and I estimate a low chaos to hover anywhere around 20-25 hours so the length is fairly good.
The new powers are pretty great and the upgrading system for them has gone more in depth since the previous game which i really liked a lot. Most powers now have 2 branches you can upgrade and, hunting for all of the runes in the levels, I found it pretty easy to form a play style I was most comfortable with in the gameplay. For example, you can upgrade the grip ability to grab humans so what I would do is hide in the up in the rafters and pull bad guys up with it and assassinate them up there.
Bethesda has also introduced a new enemy to the series in this installment of Dishonored: The clockwork robots. And let me tell you, these robots can be nothing but terrifying when you first encounter them and don't really know how to deal with them effectively. The first level where they were introduced was just a blast because it seemed like the perfect about of these guys in the whole level. But after this first level it kind of dissapointed me that I only saw about 5 in the rest of the game after that because there would be some spots in there where they would be perfect.
The stealth in this game is a lot like the previous game
and for Dishonored veterans like me, it will be very easy to pick up on quickly. It just feels easy to be able to hide up in the rafters and evade enemies.
Combat is not something i had to deal with much because i was trying to stay stealthy but in the moments i did encounter it, it was very fluent and seemed well done. Though like Dishonored you have guys who will stand about 10 feet away from you and shoot at you, this doesn't seem to happen as often which is an improvement. The swordplay is alright but it seems harder to block now.
Overall i would strongly reccomend this game because it feels good running and is very fun. If you do notice framerate issues with low graphics maybe try getting it for a console instead of PC because this was an amazing experience for any dishonored fan.

I played the mod some time ago and waited for a sale before buying the steam version. Seems I was correct since these two don't differ much at first glance. Xen is still missing, how long has it been now? I understand the devs wanting Xen to be perfect, but 3 years and counting come on..
Personal issues aside, if you love half life as much as me this mod/game is a must play. The level design is beautifull, with every original level recreated in source with lovelingly attention to detail. The sound is great, the music is great, the weapons and animations feel like those of the original game. I especially love the moment where you pick up the alien hivegun and I'm sure you will too.
Some of the places that weren't very clear objectivewise in the original game, have been improved. I remember not finding the fuel and such in blast pit, alot more clear now. Also less 'interesting' levels like residue processing, with the conveyer belts maze actually look like a functioning facility now instead of an excuse to go platform jumping. Every level has believable paths and doors ( some of them closed obviously ) so that it actually feels like a huge facility people work in ( or used too :p ). The puzzles have been improved here and there as well and powering up the generator ( I think blast pit ? ) is no longer a strange deathtrap, which improves the immersion immensely.
If I had to name a couple of downsides, the difficulty curve can be very random. One section you're blazing through, the other you reload 10 - 20 times because you have 20 health and those alien grunts instagib you in a second. Usually the health pack placement is good, excellent even. But I've had times where I was swimming in health but didn't need it, others I was begging the game for a healthkit but had to retry 10 times to headshot a marine 200 yards away that kept instakilling me. Health and hev suit power drains FAST in Black mesa and it's a good thing. Just be prepared to die more then in your average modern fps game, that's coming from a guy playing on normal.
Also sometimes AI would get 'stuck' for no apparent reason. For instance a vortigaunt or marine would see me, start shooting. I would duck into cover, after peeking out again they did not do anything untill I shot at them. This made some encounters a little too easy and it has to be a bug, but one I did not remember from the modversion.
Charging AI was also a downside sometimes, especially for the marines. I'm hoping to see them patched to stay in cover a bit more. They are absolutely lethal aimwise and the charging shotgun marines are especially deadly. But I saw one of them leave his mg to rush me for instance, which isn't exactly tactical. More grenade usage would be nice to see as well. The charge behavior worked well on the alien soldiers though, I had them smack me to death a couple of times.
To sum it up:
+absolutely beautifull recreation of half life
+great sound/music
+plenty of content
+epic feeling of nostalgia
+deadly marines
+marines talk like actual people
-marine AI could use a little tweaking still
-difficulty fluctuates, although annoying not that bad because of quicksave.
-AI sometimes not working? ( standing still, ignoring the player, one time an npc got stuck on a wall )
-marines talk like actual people
-still no Xen
nitpicks:
-shotgun reload animation seems a little slow and hard to interrupt ( I stopped using it mostly because of the rushing marines killing me whilst cocking it ) Make it a more effective but with less ammo.
-vortigaunts no longer one shot kill with magnum unless headshot ( they are hunched so alot of times you miss the head, especially annoying in the lambda reactor level )
Should you buy this, I think so. If you already played the mod wait for a sale like I did. Now let's hope they fix the last bugs and add Xen before the next century. Also devs, please add back the surface tension section where the marine drops the satchel in the tunnel, it was one of my favourite half life moments.
Despite my nagging, it's a great experience and every half life fan should play this.

I really enjoyed this game, for those who enjoy touching games that give what people consider "feels", then you should play this game. The game is well developed and is excellent overall, I don't write reviews all the time, but this game definitely deserves my recommendation.
To simply put, although it is created through RPG-Maker which is a program I use, the game had it's own unique atmosphere, yes the graphics still look the same, but the character design, gameplay, combat, and story itself sets it apart from other RPG-Maker games (at least). The music is great, the gameplay is easy to master and fun to use, the combat is unique and different for a RPG-Maker game, the story is touching and excellent, the character design is Anime related and was awesome, and the overall concept of the game was incredible.
The one and only issue with the game is grammar, that is it. However it has an acceptable reason behind it, originally the game was written in Chinese(I think....) and was translated to English. So, of course there will be grammar mistakes, but the game is still well developed regardless of this issue.
The story is neat and fairly interesting, I don't want to spoil anything, so I recommend to download the fairly small(space-wise) game and play it yourself. I enjoyed the story very much, there are 3 endings to the game, two I found are fairly easy to get which is Ending #2 and Ending #3, I won't reveal anything about them, but it all depends upon which choice you make at the end of the game. I'm not sure how to get Ending #1 unfortunately.
Overall the game is excellent, it definitely receives 5+/5 stars from me. Here are a list of what tags I ended up giving it:
RPG, Touching, GDS, Story-Teller, ARPG, JRPG, and CDG.
Here's an explanation to these tags:
RPG - Role Playing Game, self explanitory.
Touching - Contains a story that was touching or moving in a way that makes you sad or happy in a way. You may reference that it gives you the "feels".
GDS - Great Developed Story, as the name suggests, the story was greatly developed and receives it's own "tag".
Story-Teller - Focuses on story development, or where the story was a key factor throughout the game, or the story was presented very nicely.
ARPG - Anime Role Playing Game, self explanitory.
JRPG - Japanese Role Playing Game, self explanitory.
CDG - Character Development Game, either you have a lot of character background developed throughout the game or the character was weak before, but becomes stronger as the game progresses. Mainly it develops the character and makes that character stronger as well as adding background information for the character, for at least the main protagonist.

This game, oh this game. It is and will always be my favorite game. The graphics aren't the best of this game, even for the time it was released. The Inventory and Skill System is something that people today have to get used to, especially because it adds a new level of difficulty and needs micro-management (In my opinon every ego-shooter like Bioshock or Bioshock Infinite should've kept the skill and inventory system because just shooting makes the focus on the story and not the gameplay, making it an interactive movie more than a real game). What makes this game oh-so great is the atmosphere, the lighting is fitting, the music extremely well placed (exluding the fighting music; you will notice why), the fighting are a little dusty but still great, the audio logs just add to the experience and the story unfolds itself at a rather slow pace. The Psi-Powers (The Plasmids from Bioshock are comparable to that, tho the Plasmids are a straight downgrade in complexity) and the different kinds of weapons offer a big role playing aspect and the different types of ammo and different types of enemies were a sensation for that type
It is arguable that the second half of the game is worse than the first half, just because they built up such a tight package of atmosphere and story which is not really possible to unfold in a satisfying way. But this game is a milestone as was System Shock 1 (available on the internet, look for System Shock Portable), Doom, Quake and even Half-Life in their times.
This game is recommendable in any way, if you like Bioshock, if you like Deus Ex, if you like a good atmosphere, if you like a good story. Whatever you are looking for in System Shock 2, it will very probably not disapoint you.

System Shock 2 is a sci-fi role-playing first person shooter with rogue-like gameplay elements. The game has a really gloomy yet thrilling atmosphere where your - a cybernetically modified soldier - task is to discover what happened to your ship and find a way to escape. While this seems pretty overused, the game itself is very diverse and has some really sweet twists.
Basically you wander around on various decks of the Von Braun – a “Faster Than Lightspeed” ship – while trying to avoid or elliminate the genetically and mechanically modified creatures who roam the corridors. Even though it has scary moments, the fear itself that emenates from the very essence of the place is what makes you mad. You don't have your regular jumpscares here, but a high level of mental pressure instead.
The game is a mix of a bunch of genres. Basically a first person shooter with additional role-playing elements, however it has lots of rogue-like and puzzle-solving parts. The story – which partially can be learned through loads of audio logs – has some really nice twists also.
System Shock 2 is a lasting piece. Recommended for everyone who likes exploring huge, dark and gripping nightmares.

Pros:
1.  Good physics.  Makes me feel like I am riding on water.
2.  Variety of waves.  There are 5 locations, and each has a distinct type of of wave, with the different waves being best suited to different types of tricks.
3.  There are 24 different advanced air tricks that you can perform. Each trick takes a different amount of time to execute, and requires a certain amount of speed. Cons
1. Only 5 locations
2. Basic character face/hair/skin customization.
3.  Background is fairly plain.
I'm still enjoying it, and still trying to pull off an 11 Trick Combo. :)

I used to play Kelly Slater's Pro Surfer and Transworld Surf and loved those games. I also am a surfer myself, so I can relate to the gameplay. I was particularly excited about this game, as there hasn't been a surfing game in almost 15 years or so.
When I first played this game, I was awestruck with the amazing graphics. The water texture and wave visuals are excellent. Far better than any surfing game in the past. I'm not sure if they are completely up to what technology can do in these days, but they are fantastic and look really amazing.
The gameplay is fun and very much focused on the "trick" system. What this game is about is to do trick moves, and many of them, in all sorts and shapes. Some look impossible, but still not quite over the top. It took my a while to figure it out, but after 20 minutes I had almost everything down and this was the time when I was really sucked into the gameplay. It's great that you can do amazing tricks right out of the gate and not have to wait until you unlock them step by step. BTW, the camera angles when doing a trick really make it look awesome.
I think the tricks overall are super fun (Barrels, Aerials, Face-Tricks) and it keeps me coming back for more.
The surfing locations are great, I can definitly feel the level of difficulty and the nuances and characteristics of each wave - nicely done! However, I couldn't really notice or feel a difference between the size of the waves. The different times a day (night/day/sunset/dawn) bring a lot of visual variety and it looks absolutely stunning.
My favorite part of this game is the controls. I think it's awesome to be able to press the trick button combination without time pressure, ahead of hitting the lip/jump. For a Kick Flip you press X, Y, A. But you don't have to press them at once at the right time, but rather press them one after another before you're doing the actual trick. This gives you plenty of time to get the button combination right, before you're hitting the lip of the wave to do the actual trick. This is such a welcome improvement compared to most trick based gameslike tony hawk pro skater, skate 3, etc. It helps with the flow of the gameplay, instead of having to focus on one moment in time and hit all the buttons in that very moment. Also, it requires a bit practice to find the right "path" to steer through the waves in order to gain speed. If you are a surfer in real life, you might be at an advantage. This part has been realistically implemented. You can feel the spots on the wave where you gain speed or lose momentum. You could even "fall out" of the wave, just like in real life. This is very well executed and keeps this game fresh! Tip for non-surfers: Watch some surf videos and look at how the surfers move on the wave, e.g. before taking off on an aerial or a big move.
I hope there will be more DLC or something like that in the future. A two player split-screen would be great as well, e.g. surfing a real heat against someone and being in the same surf spot. Maybe bring in paddling, duck-diving, or even jetski pickup? It would also be nice to have more tricks in the barrel on on the face, e.g. the coffin, roof grab, etc. or nice face tricks like rail to rail carve, roundhouse cutback, etc. or even a layback bottom turn.
Bottom line, this game is a lot of fun. I'm so glad there is another surfing game taking advantage of newer graphics hardware and physics engines, it simply looks amazing. The trick system is probably the best part of this game, and the comprehensive customizations for surfer and gear keeps you coming back.  My expectations were kind of high after such long time without a surfing game, and I can say that I'm very pleased with the result. Can't put this game down! Thank you Climax Studios!
I would recommend this game to anyone interested in trick-based Skateboard, Snowboard, etc. games. This is a must buy for any surfer.

Surf World Series is the best surfing game I've ever played...
...which isn't saying much, but if a surfing game interests you, you can do a lot worse than this for $15.
It's simple, arcadey gameplay with a host of different challenges to do.
Customization is incredible right from the start and by playing you only unlock more stuff.
Controls take a bit to get used to, but are pretty intuitive once you do, and becomes second nature carving into the wave.
Soundtrack is varied and perfectly fitting.
You can put neon LED's onto your surfboard. Frankly it's worth a buy just for this.
On the other hand, though;
The game has a tendency to crash pretty often, at least for me and a friend I played with. Usually a crash every hour or two.
Multiplayer is bare-bones as it gets. You never get to actually surf *with* other players, nor is there any sort of interaction. You basically just play a challenge at the same time and at the end the game informs you who won. It works, but it would have been cool to see neon trails crossing each other on a single wave...
Controls aren't nearly as workable if you don't have a controller. Most games I vastly prefer keyboard, but for this one I just had to cave and use a gamepad.
There really isn't any variety in the gameplay other than 'ride a single wave towards the camera'. It does that very well, but if you're hoping for a ton of different modes and styles you'd expect from a $80 release, you're not going to be thrilled.
Bottom line is, well, if you want to surf in a video game I couldn't suggest anything better than this. For the $15 price-point, you'd certainly be getting your money's worth. It won't rob hundreds of hours of your life, and there's really no way to mellow out and surf about with your friends, but if you just want to surf, I heartily reccommend it.

I am a huge fan of the first Dishonored game, but after reading lots of negative reviews regarding how this game is a bad port, I was very hesitant to purchase Dishonored 2. I did not own the game at its release so I do not know how terrible the port is on the first couple days after the release, but since Betheda released the 1.2 patch that is supposed to fix the problems, I decided to give the game a try.
Specs:
i5 4690k 3.5GHz
GTX 970
8GB RAM
Game is installed on a regular hardrive (non-SSD) and overall the loads and reloads are fairly fast. I have put the graphics on High (there is Very High and Ultra above it) and turned on the special effects (Godrays, etc.) and the game runs at mid-70s FPS. In my 9ish hours of gameplay the game did crash twice, but with autosave it didn't really cause any troubles. Overall, I believe the devs has fixed the problem and the game is definitely playable at this moment.
Now about the game.
It's amazing and I love it. Of course the "take back what's yours" storyline isn't new, but so far I am enjoying the story even though I am only on mission 4/10 (I think?). Your abilities vary depending on who you choose, but every single ability can be further improved and upgraded on multiple levels by using runes. The graphics and Emily/Corvo's actions are very smooth and a lot more stunning, and there are so many ways to pass/bypass a certain objective that you will not feel restricted to one playstyle and you can certainly develop your own. The city of Karnaca is beautiful, voice acting is on point. On top of that, you get to craft your own bonecharms and even runes!
I am very pleased with this game, and if I have to be very picky I would say that sometimes the narrations/dialogues end on a very awkward statement/sentence, reminds me of myself talking to girls in middle school.
Great game 9/10 definitely would recommend given that you computer has no trouble running it.
Major bug: The Strong Arms bonecharm is supposed to reduce the time it takes to choke an enemy, but the bug makes it take even longer to render someone unconscious, so do not equip that particular bonecharm until update.

System Shock 2 is from the producers who would eventually make Bioshock years later. What makes System Shock 2 so special is that it was the predecessor for modern fps games. I can't think of any bad things about this game. System Shock 2 is the progressive title that modernized and ushered in a new era of FPS games. If you like atmospheric FPS, I highly recommend System Shock 2. This is the pinnacle of the genre. System Shock 2 takes about 15 hours to complete.

One of those classics that hasn't aged well at all.  As demonstrated in the Thief games, the dark engine can pull off stealth beautifully, however it falters when it comes to straight up combat (it's floaty, awkward, and really doesn't work as an FPS engine).  Thief 2 wisely avoided combat entirely for this reason, but unfortunately too much of "System Shock 2" is just straight up combat. The early portions of the game when you are just getting your bearings and exploring the ship level by level are entertaining enough, but as the game progresses it turns into a much more tedious corridor shooter.  Ammo is scarce, enemies are repetitive and, even worse, they repeatedly respawn. Like Thief, the levels are massive and thus easy to get lost in, but unlike Thief they are not all that varied or well designed.  And as the game progresses too much of your time is spent back tracking over areas you've already covered on tedious object hunts which usually don't amount to much more than cleverly disguised "find the red, blue, green, etc, etc keys to advance" style of game play that used to be 1990s FPS' stock and trade.
There are some brilliant ideas here (it has tons of atmosphere, the scarcity of ammo really creates a palpable sense of desperation and fear at times, and Shodan is one of the most memorable and influential video game villains ever for reasons that would probably be too spoilery to go into), but for all its innovation and clever ideas unfortunately the core game play just isn't that fun.

A love letter to the original 1979 science fiction film.  Painstaking attention to detail, from the construction of the environments to the audio and soundtrack/score.  Whenever possible, it seems the developers used assets from 20th Century Fox.  Jerry Goldsmith's score is used throughout, and the original cast (minus Ian Holm) return to lend their voices to audio logs.
The gameplay is great, if a bit tiring in this lengthy campaign.  Luckily, by the end you should have a decent collection of goodies to make evading yet another roomful of enemies less frustrating.
If you're a fan of the original film, play this game.

Score: 9 / 10
Price/Value: $40-
Time: 18 hours (Incl. minor ID tag/log hunting)
**Does not include Crew Expendable / DLC yet** (Have not played it)
Well folks, we've been waiting for an excellent Alien game and here it is! Fans of things like Amnesia, Outlast, Penumbra, etc will find a common game mechanic in hiding as your main form of defense. You -do- get some weapons and tools but I will get into those a little later.
You play Amanda Ripley, daughter of Ellen Ripley from the original film. You are looking for the blackbox from the Nostromo which you heard was recently recovered in search of your mother. This opens up some nice Nostromo logs which help reference the original film more.
You spend most of the game either hiding from the alien or combating androids.
Weapons such as a stun baton, maintenance jack, revolver, shotgun and boltgun are all effective against androids. The alien is best combated via stealth and planned movement. A handful of distractions and saves exist versus the alien...noisemakers, flares, smoke bombs, etc...which I found I never used. Molotovs and the flamethrower cause the alien to retreat into the nearest vent giving you roughly 3 - 5 seconds of freedom to move before the alien returns.
Gameplay-wise there is nothing special here. It's the world that Alien takes place in that makes the game amazing. From the growls of the alien on the prowl to the glow of android eyes models are fantastic to look at. Key animations and movements from the original film make an appearance that Alien fans will enjoy. The motion tracker is solid and easy to read. The station, derelict, space and vent ducts are all highly authentic to the universe and feel like you are stepping into it yourself.
I was highly reserved coming into this so I was pleasently surprised with how entertained I was. Aside from ID tag / log hunting this game really is a one shot wonder like most story games. I definitely recommend picking it up for $40 or less. The value is there and this might end up being my Game of the Year.
